title: Peripheral immune influences on the brain: adaptive immune T and B cells regulate cognitive dysfunction.
abstract: Cognitive dysfunction is recognized as one of the most concerning complications in aging as well as in disease states such as neurodegenerative disorders and stroke. Although previous studies mainly focused on local brain pathology, growing evidence highlights neuroimmune crosstalk as a key regulator of cognitive function. In particular, bidirectional communication between peripheral adaptive immunity and the central nervous system (CNS) has emerged as an important mechanism underlying cognitive dysfunction. T- and B-cell subsets exert distinct effects on cognitive regulation, ranging from maintaining homeostasis to driving neuroinflammation and dysfunction. Following blood-brain barrier disruption, peripheral lymphocytes infiltrate the CNS and reshape the neuroinflammatory microenvironment through interactions with distinct glial cells. In parallel, meningeal immunity and lymphatic drainage have been identified as critical interfaces linking peripheral and central immune responses in cognitive regulation. In this review, we summarize the multifaceted roles of adaptive immune T and B cells in cognitive dysfunction, with particular emphasis on their subset-specific features, their crosstalk with glial cells, and the contribution of meningeal immunity. We further discuss the potential underlying mechanisms, with the aim of providing insights that may inform therapeutic strategies for cognitive dysfunction.

title: Females show less hypoxia-induced blood-brain barrier disruption in aged mice: a protective role for CD11c.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
abstract: Aging is associated with a decline in blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity. Interestingly, recent reports suggest that females may be more resistant to BBB disruption than males. Using a robust model of hypoxia-induced BBB disruption, we exposed aged (20 months) male and female mice to chronic mild hypoxia (CMH; 8% O2) for 4 days before evaluating BBB disruption and endothelial proliferation by immunofluorescent (IF) analysis. Bulk RNA-seq analysis was used to identify differentially expressed genes between male and female brains. Function-blocking antibody studies then evaluated the role of an identified candidate protein, CD11c. Compared with aged male mice, females show reduced levels of hypoxia-induced BBB disruption and endothelial proliferation. Bulk RNA-seq identified Itgax, which encodes the adhesion protein CD11c as the only gene showing a greater than 2-fold difference (higher in female) between the sexes. IF analysis of brain tissue revealed that CD11c is expressed predominantly by microglia and confirmed its higher expression in females. In the hypoxic brain, CD11c+ microglia co-localized with vascular disruptions. Functional blockade of CD11c in females resulted in elevated BBB disruption and endothelial proliferation that was associated with enhanced microglial and vascular activation, culminating in reduced density of mature oligodendrocytes. Our data provide further evidence that the female brain is better equipped to withstand BBB disruption and suggest that the microglial receptor CD11c may play a protective role in maintaining BBB integrity.

title: Spinal dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate induces convulsion-like behavior via NMDA receptor-mediated Ca2+ influx and sigma-1 receptor-mediated intracellular Ca2+ release.
abstract: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) is a neurosteroid that modulates spinal nociception and hyperalgesia. However, the immediate impact of an acute increase in spinal DHEAS remains poorly understood. Here, we report that intrathecal (i.t.) administration of DHEAS (0.3-10 nmol) dose-dependently induces an abrupt, transient convulsion-like behavior lasting approximately 5 min in mice, whereas its unconjugated form DHEA exhibits no such effect. This behavior was significantly attenuated by pre-treatment with either the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 or the sigma-1 receptor (Sig-1R) antagonist BD1047, and almost completely abolished by their co-administration. Although the L-type Ca2+ channel blocker nifedipine had no effect on DHEAS-induced behavior, ruling out voltage-gated Ca2+ influx, combination experiments with specific Ca2+ modulators revealed distinct underlying mechanisms. The inhibitory effect of the extracellular Ca2+ chelator EGTA was synergistically potentiated when combined with BD1047, but showed no additive effect with MK-801. Conversely, depletion of intracellular Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin produced robust synergistic inhibition with MK-801, but not with BD1047. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that an acute increase in spinal DHEAS triggers transient convulsion-like behavior via dual-source Ca2+ signaling (extracellular influx via NMDA receptors and intracellular release via Sig-1Rs), highlighting calcium source-dependent mechanisms underlying neurosteroid-induced spinal hyperexcitability.

title: Prognostic value of admission ionized calcium and acidosis in severely injured trauma patients.
journal: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine
abstract: The association between ionized calcium (iCa²⁺) levels at admission and mortality in trauma patients remains controversial, with prior studies suggesting increased mortality in both hypocalcemic and hypercalcemic states. This study aimed to characterize the relationship between admission iCa²⁺ and key clinical outcomes, including mortality, and to clarify the contribution of acidosis-particularly among patients presenting with elevated iCa²⁺ levels. We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study using a trauma registry (2011-2021). Adult trauma patients admitted to a level-1 trauma center with measured admission iCa²⁺ were included. Hypocalcemia and hypercalcemia were defined as iCa²⁺ 1.20 mmol/L, respectively. The primary outcome was mortality at hospital discharge (MHD); secondary outcomes were massive transfusion and trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC). Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. We additionally assessed whether incorporating pH-adjusted iCa²⁺ improved the predictive performance of the mortality model. Among 977 patients (93% blunt trauma; median ISS 25 [IQR 17-33]), hypocalcemia was observed in 291 (30%) and hypercalcemia in 80 (8%). In multivariable analysis, hypocalcemia was independently associated with MHD (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.02-2.85) and TIC (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.58-3.18), but not with massive transfusion. Incorporating pH-adjusted iCa²⁺ did not improve model performance (AUC 0.937, 95% CI 0.920-0.952 vs. 0.940, 95% CI 0.922-0.954 with unadjusted iCa²⁺) for predicting MHD, whereas pH-adjusted hypocalcemia was independently associated with 24-hours mortality (OR 5.35, 95% CI 2.70-10.60), as was pH 1.20 mmol/L appears largely attributable to profound metabolic acidosis and shock. Recognizing this acidosis-driven elevation in iCa²⁺ may help anticipate the subsequent decline in iCa²⁺ that can occur as pH normalizes during resuscitation.

title: Disease-specific dominant signalling pathways and signatures in cerebrovascular diseases.
abstract: Cerebrovascular diseases (CVDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of brain diseases, including stroke, cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD), cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), and vascular dementia (VaD), driven by distinct yet overlapping vascular and cellular mechanisms. Advances in molecular medicine and omics technologies have identified disease-specific dominant signalling pathways and molecular signatures that govern disease initiation, progression, and clinical outcomes, offering a basis for precision therapeutics. In acute CVDs, ischaemic stroke is characterised by abrupt hypoperfusion activating hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF-1α), glutamate-NMDA receptor excitotoxicity, stress-activated MAPK cascades, NF-κB- and inflammasome-mediated sterile inflammation, and PI3K/Akt-mTOR survival signalling, forming a dynamic injury-repair continuum. Haemorrhagic stroke is dominated by blood-derived signalling, including thrombin-protease-activated receptor activation, haemoglobin/haem-TLR4 signalling, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, matrix metalloproteinase-mediated extracellular matrix degradation, and complement activation, leading to rapid blood-brain barrier disruption and amplified innate immune responses. Chronic CVDs exhibit sustained neurovascular dysfunction. CSVD is defined by endothelial nitric oxide dysregulation, TGF-β/SMAD overactivation, NOTCH3 signalling abnormalities, and pericyte-endothelial uncoupling, supporting a vascular-first paradigm. CAA involves amyloid-β deposition impairing vascular clearance and promoting chronic inflammation, while VaD arises from prolonged hypoperfusion, endothelial stress, oxidative injury, and low-grade inflammation, culminating in progressive cognitive decline. Overall, delineating disease-specific signalling networks and molecular signatures across acute and chronic CVDs enables biomarker discovery, phase-specific therapeutic targeting, and neurovascular unit-focused interventions, providing a unified framework for advancing precision strategies to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Trends in WHOQOL-BREF and EUROHIS-QOL-8 health-related quality of life scores among the Thai population from the 1990s to 2023: an application of Rasch analysis.
abstract: The World Health Organization Quality of Life-brief (WHOQOL-BREF) and the EUROHIS-QOL-8, an abridged version of WHOQOL-BREF, tools have been used widely in Thailand to assess health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in the general population. The availability of data spanning multiple time points now presents an opportunity to explore long-term trends in HRQoL scores and examine whether Thai respondents' interpretations of questionnaire items have changed over time. Therefore, the primary objective of this study was to examine long-term trends of WHOQOL-BREF scores collected at three time points. Analyses of differential item functioning (DIF) were also performed to investigate whether Thai individuals interpreted and endorsed WHOQOL-BREF domains/items and EUROHIS-QOL-8 items consistently across time to support the validity of these comparisons. This study conducted Rasch analysis on small, randomly selected Bangkok-only subsamples (n = 150 per time point) from three datasets (n = 300 in 1990s, n = 1200 in pre-COVID 2019, and n = 2000 in post-COVID 2023) using the WHOQOL-BREF and EUROHIS-QOL-8 instruments. DIF explored temporal changes in item interpretation across age, sex, and dataset. Mean HRQOL scores derived from four WHOQOL-BREF domains and EUROHIS-QOL-8 increased across the three time points; however, social and environmental domains did not show any statistically significant difference (p > 0.05). DIF revealed that physical and psychological domains were more difficult to score high for the samples from the 1990s compared to those from the two time periods, whereas social and environmental domains displayed an opposite effect. Although these findings highlight the increasing HRQoL trends in Bangkok and suggest the importance of considering societal changes when interpreting long-term HRQoL data, an investigation with a nationally representative sample of Thai population is warranted for future studies to confirm these findings.

title: Genome-wide diversity of Chinese Sinan and Xiangxi beef cattle populations based on whole-genome resequencing.
abstract: This study conducted analysis of genetic diversity, population structure, and selection signatures in Sinan cattle (SNC) and Xiangxi cattle (XXC) using whole-genome resequencing data. SNC and XXC cattle are indigenous beef populations in southwestern China, with ongoing conservation and breeding programs managed by their respective original breeding farms. Whole-genome sequencing of 28 SNC and 23 XXC individuals achieved an average depth of 12.3× (SD = 1.4) and 12.8× (SD = 1.6), respectively. Using genome-wide SNP data (mean MAF 0.1034-0.1080, PIC 0.1257-0.1312), we found that XXC exhibited significantly higher observed heterozygosity than SNC (Ho = 0.1275 vs. 0.1195, t-test p < 0.01) and faster LD decay, indicating greater genetic diversity. ADMIXTURE cross-validation showed K = 1 as optimal (highest likelihood, lowest CV error), indicating no significant stratification; K = 7 revealed subtle differentiation (ΔK = 42.3), suggesting incipient divergence. Selection signature analysis employed pairwise Fst and θπ ratio (top 5% as threshold). We identified 1,315 significant genomic regions, comprising 1,993 candidate genes in SNC and 1,407 in XXC. Only 218 genes (12.9%) were shared between the two populations, indicating divergent selection pressures. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that PI3K-Akt (P = 0.003) and MAPK (P = 0.008) pathways were significantly enriched in SNC, while tuberculosis (P = 0.015) and AMPK (P = 0.021) pathways were significantly enriched in XXC. GO enrichment analysis, after Benjamini‑Hochberg correction (FDR < 0.05), showed that SNC genes were significantly enriched in actin cytoskeleton (GO:0015629, P = 0.009) and mitochondrial membrane (GO:0031966, P = 0.013), whereas XXC genes were significantly enriched in synaptic structure (GO:0098794, P = 0.024) and dendritic development (GO:0097447, P = 0.031). These functional divergences likely reflect population‑specific adaptations. This work establishes a genomic foundation for future association studies and marker-assisted selection in these two important indigenous populations.

title: Highly active sulfate-reducing bacteria drive biogenic souring in oil reservoirs: insights from metabolic capability and microbial interactions.
abstract: In reservoir microbiome, sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominate the biogeochemical cycling of sulfur elements. As the main biological source of hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) in oil reservoirs, SRB also cause substantial economic losses in oil reservoirs. Effective souring control requires a deeper understanding of SRB activity, especially the highly efficient H₂S-producing strains. However, current studies have largely emphasized community-level analysis, leaving the role of key SRB species and their interactions with other functional microorganisms poorly resolved. Firstly, integrated metagenomic and culture-based analyses of the original samples from Chengbei Oilfield revealed temperature as the key factor shaping SRB structure, and the highest H₂S production rates were observed under high-temperature conditions (60 °C). Within the SRB community, we proposed that highly active-rather than abundant-SRB were the primary drivers of biogenic H₂S production. Although Desulfofundulus and Desulfotomaculum represented only 3.13% and 6.41% of the community, respectively, their presence strongly correlated with H₂S accumulation (p 1000 ppm H₂S in 3 days, but less than in lactate medium (> 2000 ppm/24 h); Desulfotomaculum sp. 45-6 demonstrated limited alkane degradation and could produce < 1000 ppm H₂S only supplemented with methanol or lactate. Their respective roles and contribution to ecosystem functions, particularly H₂S production, is not equivalent. Our findings establish that metabolic activity, not relative abundance, is the key predictor of the environmental impact of SRB. This study provides a mechanistic understanding of reservoir souring by identifying metabolically dominant taxa and synergistic interactions within microbial communities, offering a trait-based framework for developing targeted souring management strategies. title: Eating disorder symptoms, perceived stress, insomnia, and cognitive-behavioral avoidance in university students with bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder.
abstract: Eating disorder symptoms frequently co-occur with mood, obsessive-compulsive, trauma-related, and stress-related psychopathology. Emerging evidence suggests that perceived stress, insomnia, and cognitive-behavioral avoidance may represent transdiagnostic mechanisms contributing to maladaptive eating behaviors. However, their relative contributions across psychiatric diagnostic groups remain poorly understood. This study investigated differences in eating disorder symptoms, avoidance behaviors, insomnia severity, and perceived stress among university students with self-reported Bipolar Disorder (BD), Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD), Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), and non-clinical comparison group (HCG). In this cross-sectional study, 879 university students were allocated to Bipolar Disorder (BD, n = 114), Major Depressive Disorder (MDD, n = 225), Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD, n = 184), Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD, n = 156) and non-clinical comparison group (HCG, n = 200) groups based on self-reported psychiatric diagnoses obtained through an online self-report questionnaire. Participants completed the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire-13 (EDE-Q-13), Cognitive Behavioral Avoidance Scale-Turkish Version (CBAS-TR), Bergen Insomnia Scale (BIS), and Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) during a single time-point assessment conducted between March and May 2026. Sociodemographic and clinical variables including body mass index, psychotherapy history, psychiatric medication use, and sleep duration were additionally evaluated using self-reported survey measures. Group differences were examined using one-way ANOVA, associations were evaluated using Pearson correlation analyses, and diagnostic-group-specific predictors of eating disorder symptoms were investigated using multiple linear regression models. Significant between-group differences were observed across all dimensions of eating disorder psychopathology, cognitive-behavioral avoidance, insomnia severity, and perceived stress (all p < .001). Participants with MDD and PTSD exhibited the highest levels of eating disorder symptoms, whereas HCG group consistently demonstrated the lowest scores. Avoidance behaviors, insomnia severity, and perceived stress were markedly elevated across all psychiatric groups compared with controls. Correlation analyses revealed strong positive associations within theoretically related domains, particularly among eating disorder symptoms, avoidance behaviors, insomnia indicators, and perceived stress dimensions. Multiple regression analyses demonstrated that perceived stress was the only variable independently associated with EDE-Q total scores, and this association was observed exclusively in the BD group (β = .276, p = .005). Neither insomnia severity nor cognitive-behavioral avoidance independently predicted eating disorder symptoms in any diagnostic category. University students with psychiatric diagnoses exhibit substantially greater eating pathology, avoidance tendencies, insomnia symptoms, and perceived stress than HCG group peers. Among the examined psychological factors, perceived stress was independently associated with eating disorder symptom severity only in individuals with BD group. Because of the cross-sectional design, the direction and causal nature of this association cannot be determined. These findings provide limited support for a transdiagnostic interpretation, as the independent association between perceived stress and eating disorder symptom severity was observed exclusively in the BD group. The results therefore suggest a potentially diagnosis-specific role of perceived stress rather than a consistent effect across psychiatric diagnostic groups.

title: Dual topical therapy with doxepin and allopurinol mouthwash for severe methotrexate-induced oral mucositis: a pediatric case report.
abstract: High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) is a cornerstone of chemotherapy for pediatric osteosarcoma but frequently induces severe oral mucositis, a dose-limiting toxicity characterized by painful ulceration and impaired oral function. While standard supportive care includes leucovorin rescue, hydration, and analgesics, topical agents like doxepin mouthwash offer pain relief, and allopurinol may provide mucosal protection through antioxidant effects. We report a 16-year-old male with osteosarcoma who developed World Health Organization grade 4 oral mucositis on day 3 following his first cycle of HD-MTX (10 g/m2). The symptoms included severe odynophagia, dysphagia, and extensive ulcerative lesions, necessitating partial parenteral nutrition. Treatment involved dual topical therapy with doxepin (0.5% solution) and allopurinol (1 mg/mL) mouthwashes, administered 15 mL four times daily, alongside enhanced oral hygiene and systemic analgesics. Pain scores reduced from severe to 4/10 within 48 h, with mucosal improvement by day 5 and resolution to grade 1 by day 7. No significant adverse effects were noted. In subsequent cycles, prophylactic allopurinol mouthwash minimized or prevented mucositis recurrence despite higher MTX doses. This single case is suggestive of a possible role for combined doxepin and allopurinol mouthwashes for managing severe high-dose MTX-induced oral mucositis in adolescents. Mechanistically supported by doxepin's analgesic properties and allopurinol's antioxidant and metabolic modulation, this dual approach merits further evaluation in randomized controlled trials to optimize supportive care in pediatric oncology.

title: Perineural invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: clinical evidence and mechanistic hypotheses.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence in cancer neuroscience suggests that tumor-nerve crosstalk can modulate tumor growth, immune remodeling, dissemination, and therapy resistance. Perineural invasion (PNI) is a hallmark of aggressive tumors and correlates with recurrence, metastasis, disease-specific death, and neuropathic pain, yet its prevalence and prognostic relevance in primary HCC remain inconsistently defined. Given the limited and heterogeneous clinical data, we synthesize available observations and propose mechanistic hypotheses for neural-tumor interactions in the hepatic niche. Potential drivers are organized into five domains-neurotrophic factors, axon guidance molecules, neurotransmitter signaling, cell adhesion molecules, and the tumor microenvironment-highlighting neuro-immune-stromal circuits that may create permissive perineural niches. We also outline experimental platforms to test these hypotheses, including co-culture systems, organoids, and microfluidic nerve-on-chip models. Targeting neural-tumor interactions may offer translational opportunities in HCC, but causality and actionable targets cannot be established without improved clinical and experimental rigor. Standardized pathological assessment and dedicated HCC-focused PNI models are needed to validate mechanisms, harmonize reporting, and enable reproducible, clinically meaningful advances.

title: Tissue-specific metabolic profiles and volatile chemodiversity in Camellia ptilophylla: a survey of 16 individuals and eight tissues.
abstract: Camellia ptilophylla is a rare and endemic tea germplasm resource in China, valued for its low or zero caffeine and high theobromine content. However, its morphological traits, biochemical differences among individuals, tissue-specific metabolite distribution patterns, and volatile compounds have not been systematically reported. In this study, we quantified morphological traits and the contents of catechins, theanine, alkaloids, and volatile compounds in individual plants and across different tissues (roots, fruit, semi-lignified stems, lignified stems, one bud with one leaf, second leaf, third leaf, and mature leaf). Most individual C. ptilophylla plants contained no caffeine, with an average theobromine content of 34.4 mg/g. Gallocatechin gallate (GCG) was the dominant catechin, accounting for 54% of the total catechin content. Caffeine showed the highest inter-individual variation, while GCG was the most consistent. Catechins and caffeine accumulated mainly in young shoots and declined with leaf age, and theanine was detected only in roots (mean 12.96 mg/g). A total of 89 volatile compounds were detected, with (E)-2-hexenal, linalool, methyl salicylate and benzaldehyde as the dominant contributors, conferring predominantly floral and fruity aroma notes. This study provides the systematic profiling of volatile chemodiversity in C. ptilophylla, demonstrating individual-associated aroma variation, and establishes a comprehensive tissue-level metabolic map across eight organs, confirming that theanine was detected exclusively in roots of the three individuals examined. These findings open new possibilities for flavor-oriented breeding and chemotype-guided utilization of this unique plant resource.

title: The neurocognitive cost of media multitasking: fragmented screens, fragmented minds!
abstract: As "digital natives," Generation Z university students rely heavily on mobile devices across all life domains. Diverging from the literature's historical focus on total screen time, this study aimed to objectively characterize the entire digital footprint (including duration, fragmentation, and content type) and investigate how these patterns are associated with cognitive control. We conducted a cross-sectional digital phenotyping study with 206 health sciences students. Objective 7-day smartphone logs were integrated with a custom mobile Stroop task completed on participants' own devices to ensure high ecological validity. A clinical battery assessed sleep quality, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) symptoms, anxiety, headache, neck disability, and computer vision syndrome. The Cumulative Digital Load Score was developed and compared with objective device metrics. Theory-driven family-based correlation analyses (13 FDR-corrected tests) examined screen pattern-Stroop associations, and trial-level Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMMs) isolated momentary predictor effects across 12,035 trials. Objective data revealed a highly intensive and fragmented digital profile: a median of 6.6 h of daily screen time, 142 pickups, an average session duration of 2.9 min, and a 40% passive consumption ratio. Family-based analyses demonstrated that fragmentation metrics were significantly associated with conflict resolution costs (FDR q < 0.05). LMMs revealed that raw total screen time did not predict cognitive accuracy. The models identified two distinct impairment profiles: high digital attention fragmentation was associated with selective weakening of proactive conflict control (increasing errors specifically on incongruent trials), whereas clinical/somatic symptom burden and ADHD symptomatology were associated with a broader accuracy cost that, particularly for somatic pain burdens, extended even to highly automated congruent trials. Convergence between the self-reported CDLS and the objective device logs was weak (ρ ≈ 0.14-0.18), indicating that the two capture related but distinct aspects of digital behaviour rather than interchangeable estimates of the same construct. Digital exposure does not cause a single, homogenous cognitive deficit. Highly fragmented use, characterized by constant interruptions and short session durations, is associated with poorer proactive cognitive control and a specific accuracy cost. Passive consumption is associated with block-dependent processing delays without affecting highly automatic cognitive tasks. Because the two blocks were administered in a fixed order, this contrast is confounded with task order and practice. These findings suggest that cognitive health in the digital age may benefit from targeted "digital hygiene" strategies prioritizing the minimization of attention fragmentation, rather than solely focusing on screen time reduction.

title: Yangxue Qingnao attenuates nitroglycerin-induced chronic migraine-like pain in association with altered mitochondrial calcium handling and reduced TNC neuronal excitability.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Chronic migraine is characterized by recurrent trigeminovascular activation, cutaneous allodynia, and central sensitization. Mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired calcium handling may contribute to migraine chronification, but whether these processes are modified by Yangxue Qingnao (YXQN), a traditional Chinese medicine used for headache disorders, remains unclear. Here, a chronic migraine mouse model was induced by intraperitoneal nitroglycerin (NTG) injections on alternate days for 9 days. Migraine-like behaviors, trigeminal nucleus caudalis (TNC) neuropeptide expression, neuronal activation, proteomic profiling, mitochondrial function, and electrophysiological properties were assessed. YXQN attenuated migraine-like phenotypes, reduced TNC calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) levels and c-Fos neuronal activation in TNC region. Proteomic analysis identified exploratory changes in mitochondrial- and calcium-transport-related pathways. YXQN treatment was accompanied by improvements in selected mitochondrial structural and functional measures, reduced calcium-associated fluorescence signals, and attenuated TNC neuronal hyperexcitability. These findings support further investigation of mitochondrial calcium handling and TNC neuronal excitability as potential contributors to the effects of YXQN.

title: IL-17A/IL-17RA signaling drives microglial mtDNA-cGAS/STING axis to promote synaptic and cognitive impairment in chronic migraine.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Cognitive dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to disability in chronic migraine (CM), yet the mechanisms linking neuroinflammation to synaptic dysfunction and cognitive decline remain poorly understood. Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) has emerged as an important regulator of neuroimmune interactions in neurological disorders; however, its role in migraine-associated cognitive impairment remains unknown. A nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced mouse model of CM was combined with behavioral testing, transcriptomic profiling, immunohistochemistry, molecular analyses, and in vitro microglial studies. IL-17A neutralization, Il17ra knockdown, antioxidant treatment, and pharmacological inhibition of STING were used to dissect the underlying mechanisms. Repeated NTG administration induced mechanical hypersensitivity, cognitive impairment, and elevated cortical IL-17A expression. Neutralization of IL-17A significantly alleviated both nociceptive sensitization and cognitive deficits. Transcriptomic analyses revealed activation of IL-17 and cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways, accompanied by suppression of synaptic-related programs. Mechanistically, IL-17RA was predominantly upregulated in cortical microglia, where IL-17A promoted oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release. Cytosolic mtDNA subsequently activated the cGAS/STING pathway, driving inflammatory microglial remodeling and excessive synaptic engulfment. Pharmacological or genetic interruption of this signaling cascade attenuated cGAS/STING activation, reduced microglial inflammatory responses, and preserved synaptic integrity. Importantly, STING inhibition markedly suppressed microglial synaptic engulfment and rescued synaptic deficits in repeated NTG-treated mice. Our findings identify an IL-17A/IL-17RA-ROS-mtDNA-cGAS/STING signaling cascade in microglia that links neuroinflammation to synaptic pathology chronic migraine-like conditions. By driving inflammatory microglial remodeling and excessive synaptic pruning, this pathway contributes to migraine-associated cognitive dysfunction and represents a potential therapeutic target for preventing migraine chronification and its cognitive impairments. title: New Anti-Inflammatory Alkaloid and Potential Analgesic Constituents Isolated From Zanthoxylum dissitum.
abstract: A new alkaloid, named p-coumaroyl-histamine-N-glucoside (6), together with eight known compounds, was isolated from Zanthoxylum dissitum, a key medicinal plant of the gynecological formulation Fuke Qianjin capsule, which is used for the treatment of inflammatory disorders. The structures of all isolated compounds were determined by comprehensive spectroscopic analysis and comparison with literature data. Bioassay results in vitro revealed that compounds 5, 6, and 8 exhibited obviously inhibitory activity against nitric oxide (NO) production in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 46.1, 14.9, and 28.5 µM, respectively, compared to the standard L-NMMA value of 25.4 µM. Furthermore, compounds 1-3 were found to possess potential analgesic activity in the acetic acid‑induced writhing test in mice, as revealed by fraction activity profiling.

title: Dose-Dependent Stabilization of Resting-State Neural Dynamics by Transcranial Photobiomodulation.
abstract: Transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) has shown promise in cognitive enhancement; however, its neural mechanisms remain unclear. Across three double-blind, sham-controlled electroencephalography (EEG) experiments (n = 101), we systematically characterized how right frontal tPBM modulates resting-state neural dynamics across doses. Moderate-dose tPBM most effectively stabilized resting brain states by counteracting the spontaneous slowing of individual alpha peak frequency and the shift in the aperiodic spectral slope that typically arise during quiet wakefulness. This stabilization was dose dependent, with a specific irradiance-duration combination (150 mW/cm2, 960 s) producing the most robust modulation. Moreover, frontal tPBM preserved functional connectivity and suppressed slow-wave buildup linked to drowsiness, reflecting sustained large-scale coordination and resistance to rest-related cortical drift. Together, these findings establish dose-dependent stabilization of resting-state neural dynamics as a key mechanism of tPBM and provide a physiological basis for optimizing its therapeutic application.

title: NOS3 Overexpression Enhances the Protective Effects of iPSCs and their Exosomes on Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells Injury Induced by Oxygen-Glucose Deprivation/Reperfusion.
abstract: Brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs), as the core component of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), are primary targets of ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury, leading to barrier disruption. While induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offer therapeutic potential, their efficacy is limited. Nitric oxide synthase 3 (NOS3), a key vascular endothelial regulator, is dysfunctional during I/R, but its role in enhancing iPSC therapy remains unclear. We constructed NOS3-overexpressing iPSCs and used oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) to simulate I/R injury. Cell viability, apoptosis, and differentiation were assessed via CCK-8, flow cytometry and Western blot. In vitro BBB models were established to detect TEER, sodium fluorescein permeability, and tight junction protein expression. Ferroptosis-related indicators including were analyzed using commercial assay kits and Western blot. Exosomes were isolated from iPSCs and characterized, followed by intervention experiments with exosome inhibitor heparin and NOS3 inhibitor L-NAME. In vivo, a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of NOS3-overexpressing iPSC-derived exosomes through neurological behavioral tests, TTC staining, HE staining, and immunofluorescence staining. NOS3 overexpression improved iPSCs survival and inhibited apoptosis under OGD/R. Additionally, NOS3 also promoted iPSCs differentiation into BMECs, and restored BMECs proliferation and migration following OGD/R treatment. NOS3-overexpressing iPSCs and their exosomes significantly enhanced BBB integrity, upregulated tight junction proteins expression (Claudin-5, ZO-1, Occludin), and suppressed BMECs ferroptosis compared to naive iPSCs. These protective effects were attenuated by heparin or L-NAME. In vivo, NOS3-overexpressing iPSC-derived exosomes significantly improved neurological function, reduced cerebral infarct volume, attenuated histopathological damage, increased neuronal survival, and restored ZO-1 expression in MCAO mice, with superior outcomes compared to naïve exosomes. NOS3 overexpression strengthened the protective effects of iPSCs and their exosomes against I/R-induced BBB damage by promoting iPSCs survival and differentiation, and inhibiting BMECs ferroptosis. This study identified NOS3-overexpressing iPSCs and their exosomes as promising therapeutic direction for cerebral I/R injury.

title: Restoring the perception-action cycle in frail older adults through cognitive-motor dual-task training.
abstract: Cognitive-Motor Dual-Task Training (CMDT) may promote cognitive and functional benefits in older adults; however, its effects on the neural mechanisms supporting adaptive perception-action control remain unclear. Previous analyses from the same randomized controlled trial showed that CMDT restores anticipatory control mechanisms in frail older adults. Here, we investigated whether these adaptations extend to post-stimulus stages of information processing. Thirty frail and pre-frail older adults were randomly assigned to either a CMDT group or a motor-training control group and completed an 8-week intervention. High-density electroencephalography was recorded at baseline, mid-intervention, and post-intervention while participants performed a visuomotor Go/No-go task. Analyses focused on the P1, N1, prefrontal P2 (pP2), and P3 event-related potential components. No training-related effects were observed on P1 or P3 amplitudes. In contrast, significant Group × Time interactions emerged for N1 and pP2. The CMDT group showed progressive increases in N1 amplitude, suggesting enhanced attentional selection, and increased pP2 amplitude, indicating improved stimulus-response integration and perception-action coupling. No comparable changes were observed in the control group. An exploratory Perception-Action Cycle Index further revealed a robust, progressive, and individually consistent pattern of coordinated adaptation across proactive and reactive ERP markers in the CMDT group. These findings suggest that frailty-related neurocognitive vulnerability may be partially reversible through multidomain training. By linking CMDT-induced neural plasticity to coordinated proactive-reactive processing, the perception-action cycle emerges as a potential neurophysiological marker of adaptive capacity in frail aging.

title: Nanorobotics-based strategies for brain-specific drug targeting in neurological disorders.
abstract: Neurological disorders afflict over one billion individuals globally, creating an unprecedented burden on healthcare systems and society. Despite significant advances in conventional treatments, current approaches remain constrained by limitations in early detection capabilities, inadequate target-specificity, and the formidable challenge of blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration. This comprehensive review examines the convergence of nanorobotics, artificial intelligence, and neuromedicine as an integrated paradigm capable of overcoming these limitations. We analyze historical developments from Feynman's visionary concepts to contemporary functional nanoscale devices, critically evaluate the role of AI in enabling intelligent navigation and decision-making, and systematically assess nanorobotic strategies for BBB penetration and CNS targeting. Through detailed examination of propulsion mechanisms, materials biocompatibility, control algorithms, and regulatory frameworks, we identify key translational challenges and propose a roadmap for clinical implementation. This synthesis demonstrates that the integration of these three fields can enable closed-loop diagnostic-therapeutic platforms capable of real-time adaptation to dynamic physiological environments. With appropriate attention to ethical considerations, cybersecurity protocols, and equitable access, these technologies promise to revolutionize the diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders, potentially transforming patient outcomes across the spectrum of neurodegenerative diseases, brain tumors, and cerebrovascular conditions.

title: Endothelial RRM2B-dependent mitochondrial DNA signalling drives Doxorubicin-cardiotoxicity.
abstract: Doxorubicin remains a mainstay of cancer therapy, yet its clinical use is constrained by severe cardiotoxicity, classically attributed to cardiomyocyte death. Here, we identify endothelial inflammation driven by mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) turnover and release as a critical mediator of Doxorubicin-induced cardiac injury. In vivo, a standard Doxorubicin regimen activates the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway in endothelial cells before cardiomyocyte dysfunction or death occurs. Mechanistically, Doxorubicin recruits the stress-inducible ribonucleotide reductase subunit RRM2B (p53R2) that normally sustains the mitochondrial deoxyribonucleotide pool, to promote mtDNA turnover and support its release, fuelling sterile inflammation. Genetic endothelial-specific or pharmacological inhibition of mtDNA release using the clinically approved BAX inhibitor Eltrombopag attenuates endothelial inflammation and prevents Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity in vivo without compromising anticancer efficacy. These findings reveal an unrecognized proinflammatory role of RRM2B and establish endothelial inflammation as a central driver of chemotherapy-related cardiac injury, identifying the cardiac endothelium as a tractable target for cardioprotection during cancer treatment.

title: Sequential digital cognitive screening and plasma biomarkers for detection of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Digital cognitive assessments and plasma biomarkers offer a practical path toward scalable Alzheimer's disease evaluation, but their clinical value depends on how they are deployed. In 1,001 adults aged 60-85 years from the multicenter Bio-Hermes-001 cohort in the USA, including individuals without cognitive impairment and participants with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia, we tested a sequential triage workflow. The primary endpoints were identification of clinical impairment and amyloid positivity; the secondary endpoints were the proportions of participants potentially avoiding downstream neuropsychological assessment and positron emission tomography (PET). Here we show that digital cognitive screening identified clinical impairment (best area under the curve, 0.812), whereas plasma phosphorylated tau at threonine 217 and amyloid-β42/40 predicted amyloid PET positivity (best area under the curve, 0.890). A two-threshold rule-in/rule-out strategy could avoid neuropsychological follow-up in over 60% of participants and amyloid PET in up to 85% of those entering biomarker triage. These findings support a low-burden, staged workflow that could preserve specialist capacity and make Alzheimer's disease evaluation more accessible.

title: Audio long read: The world's most precious brain samples - and what they teach us about being human.
Brain area's mysterious role in speech decoded at last.
Pericyte relaxation reverses no-reflow.
Visualizing activation of the muscle acetylcholine receptor.
abstract: The muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor is the archetypal ligand-gated ion channel, initiating skeletal muscle contraction by opening its intrinsic pore in response to neurotransmitter binding. Despite its fundamental role in synaptic signaling, the transient nature of activated receptor states has obscured the structural sequence linking agonist binding to pore opening. Here, we combine rapid agonist photolysis with cryo-electron microscopy to visualize conformational states populated during activation of the human muscle receptor. We resolve five conformations spanning a closed agonist-bound state, three intermediates and a fully open, conducting state. The structures uncover a stepwise, intrinsically asymmetric gating mechanism in which unequal subunit movements drive progressive pore expansion before reaching a pseudosymmetric conductive architecture. A discrete transition in one subunit distinguishes the open activated state from the agonist-bound desensitized state, redefining the structural boundary between activation and desensitization. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that the open conformation is hydrated and supports sodium ion permeation. These findings establish the structural trajectory of muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor activation and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how heritable mutations and autoantibodies disrupt neuromuscular signaling.

title: Genome-wide association analyses of suicidality identify 77 loci and implicate subcortical brain regions and synaptic pathways.
abstract: Suicidality contributes substantially to global morbidity and mortality, yet, despite its heritability, its biological etiology remains largely elusive. Here we conducted multi-ancestry genome-wide association study meta-analyses of suicidal ideation (259,747 cases), suicide attempt (64,993 cases), suicide death (9,197 cases) and suicidal behavior (suicide attempt/death, 75,300 cases), across 54 cohorts (for example, the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, Million Veteran Program and UK Biobank). We identified 77 significant loci across meta-analyses, including 59 previously unreported for suicidality. Single-nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability ranged from 2.0% to 6.7%, and there were strong, yet incomplete, genetic correlations between suicidality phenotypes (0.70-0.88). Fine-mapping prioritized putative causal single-nucleotide polymorphisms and 20 credible genes. Enrichment analyses implicated synaptic pathways and neuronal populations predominantly in subcortical brain regions (for example, amygdala excitatory, medium spiny and hippocampal CA1-3). Together, these findings establish suicidality as a polygenic set of traits with both shared and distinct genetic influences, providing a foundation for future studies of suicide biology and etiology.

title: Making memories generalizable.
The role of circadian clock dysfunction in Alzheimer disease pathogenesis.
abstract: The circadian clock generates 24-hour rhythms in mammalian behaviour, physiology and gene expression. Fragmentation of daily activity rhythms is among the earliest clinical features of Alzheimer disease (AD), and there is accumulating evidence that circadian disruption contributes to AD pathogenesis. This Review examines the bidirectional relationship between AD pathology and the molecular circadian clock. At the cellular level, ageing and AD pathology extensively reprogramme circadian rhythms of gene expression in a cell-type-specific manner. Conversely, genetic manipulation of clock genes in defined cell populations has revealed that astrocyte and microglial clocks control glial reactivity, neuroinflammation, lysosomal function, lipid handling and the aggregation of amyloid-β, tau and α-synuclein. The circadian clock also governs brain waste clearance through its interaction with sleep, and circadian interventions (behavioural and pharmacological) modify pathology in mouse models. We close with the questions that future longitudinal human studies and cell-type-resolved experiments will need to answer.

title: Priming future aggression via vicarious experience.
Hippocampal reactivation of aversive experience promotes a slow-breathing recovery state.
abstract: Adaptive responses to threat require both defensive behaviors that minimize danger and mechanisms that restore physiological balance. The behavioral and neural substrates of such recovery processes remain poorly defined. Here, using a two-location fear conditioning paradigm in male mice, we identify a distinct slow-breathing immobility state that emerges after threat avoidance in safe parts of the environment and supports poststress recovery. This state is characterized by 2- to 4-Hz respiration and hippocampal reactivation of the aversive experience during sharp-wave ripples (SWRs). Post-task stress levels were predicted by the balance between time spent in defensive freezing and in the slow-breathing recovery state, rather than by the number of shocks received. Disruption of hippocampal SWRs reduced the occurrence of this state and increased stress levels, whereas diazepam promoted this state while suppressing SWRs, dissociating immediate physiological relief from hippocampus-dependent processes. These findings identify a brain-body recovery state that regulates stress and suggest that hippocampal reactivation contributes to emotional resilience.

title: Age-dependent progenitor switching shapes adult brown adipose tissue heterogeneity.
abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) burns chemical energy to generate heat and supports whole-body metabolism. BAT is continuously renewed from adipose progenitor cells (APCs), yet which progenitors sustain the tissue during adulthood, and how this changes with age, remain unclear. Here we show that Pdgfra+ APCs, which build BAT early in life, contribute little to its renewal in adult mice. Using single-cell analysis and lineage tracing, we identify a previously unrecognized population of Myl1-expressing APCs that emerges with age and becomes the major source of new brown fat cells in adult and middle-aged mice. These Myl1+ APC-derived adipocytes adopt a distinct metabolic state, favouring oxidative phosphorylation over glycolysis, which contributes to the metabolic heterogeneity of adult BAT. Ablating Myl1+ APC-derived adipocytes, or blocking their differentiation, reduces BAT mass and impairs glucose control. Our findings reveal an age-dependent 'progenitor switch' that drives the renewal and functional heterogeneity of adult brown fat.

title: Supramolecular protein block copolymers encode presynaptic active-zone nanolattices.
abstract: Designing biological nanomaterials with programmable geometry and function remains a central challenge in nanotechnology. Presynaptic active zones offer a biological model of nanoscale architecture as their scaffold proteins spatially organize the machinery for neurotransmitter release. Here we show that the active-zone scaffold proteins ELKS and RIM form periodic nanodot lattices upon reconstitution in non-neuronal cells, with ELKS nanodot diameters of about 60 nm and a typical lattice spacing of about 130 nm. By combining block-copolymer theory with super-resolution nanoscopy and quantitative spatial analysis of reconstituted assemblies and neuronal synapses, we identify ELKS and RIM as a minimal scaffold module sufficient to generate hexagonal lattices through orthogonal self-association coupled with specific ELKS-RIM binding. We further demonstrate that changes in scaffold stoichiometry and incorporation of client proteins, including RIMBP2 and Liprin-α3, systematically alter lattice spacing and morphology. These findings establish molecular principles underlying active-zone architecture and provide a framework for engineering self-assembling nanomaterials with programmable spatial organization.

title: SLBP-independent control of maternal histone mRNA.
abstract: Replication-dependent (RD) histones are crucial for packaging newly replicated DNA into chromatin, ensuring genome stability. In metazoans, the mRNA of RD histones is uniquely regulated through a conserved 3' stem-loop bound by stem-loop binding protein (SLBP). This allows cell-cycle-coupled regulation of these important transcripts. However, oocytes must stabilize histone mRNAs independently of the cell cycle to ensure maternal loading to support the first embryonic divisions. Here we discovered an SLBP-independent mechanism that ensures RD histone transcript stability during oogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans. This is mediated by the protein complex PETISCO, bound to the effector protein TOST-1, which directly binds the histone stem-loop region and maintains maternal histone mRNA levels during oogenesis and early embryogenesis. Loss of this mechanism disrupts histone homeostasis, leading to premature genome activation, mitotic defects and embryonic lethality. Interestingly, the same complex, PETISCO, acts in PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) biogenesis when bound to the effector PID-1, revealing an intriguing co-option of this histone mRNA homeostasis mechanism by the piRNA pathway. Our findings reveal an SLBP-independent mechanism of histone mRNA regulation, that served as a basis for the evolution of a piRNA biogenesis mechanism.

title: The metacognitive paradox of OCD: confidence is globally reduced but shows increased sensitivity to local evidence.
abstract: Confidence is a critical metacognitive signal that guides behavior. Biases in confidence, such as excessive doubt, are hallmark features of mental health disorders, especially obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Yet the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms and how they link to learning and decision-making remain elusive. We asked patients with OCD and matched healthy controls to perform a novel rule-shifting task that incorporated trial-by-trial confidence ratings. Using a Bayesian observer model as a benchmark, we identified two distinct confidence characteristics: while patients with OCD indicated lower overall confidence, their trial-by-trial confidence ratings more accurately tracked task-relevant information, rendering their confidence reports more closely aligned with the Bayesian benchmark than those of controls. These findings challenge the idea of a simple, unified metacognitive impairment in OCD. Instead, they suggest that OCD is linked to an enhanced responsiveness to environmental evidence and feedback during decision-making.

title: A large dataset of human EEG responses to short naturalistic videos for studying dynamic audio-visual event processing.
abstract: Vision neuroscience has experienced a surge in the collection and use of large-scale datasets of brain responses to naturalistic images. However, static images lack the temporal dimension essential for understanding how vision is solved in the brain during dynamic real life settings. To facilitate the study of the neural correlates of dynamic visual event perception, we introduce the EEG Moments Dataset (EMD). EMD consists of 128-channel EEG responses and eye-tracking recordings of 6 human participants viewing 1,102 short naturalistic videos (3-second long; with audio track) while maintaining central fixation. We show that EMD's EEG responses well encode stimulus-related information, exhibit a temporal correspondence with the video stimuli, and have a rich representational content revealed by brain encoding models based on different feature spaces. Furthermore, complemented by the BOLD Moments Dataset (BMD) - an existing large-scale dataset of human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) responses for the same videos - EMD enables spatio-temporally resolved investigations of brain responses to dynamic visual events. We release EMD's EEG and eye-tracking data in both raw and preprocessed format which is complemented by BMD's 1,102 video stimuli and rich stimulus metadata. Finally, we provide an interactive code tutorial to familiarize with EMD's preprocessed data, stimuli, and stimulus metadata.

title: Proprioceptive-visual disturbances in Alzheimer's disease and posterior cortical atrophy.
abstract: Diminished spatial orientation, mobility and upper limb functions are disabling consequences of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Proprioceptive disturbances are a candidate explanation for these deficits; we hypothesized these would be elevated in typical Alzheimer's disease and especially posterior cortical atrophy ('visual-spatial AD'). Participants (posterior cortical atrophy n = 25; typical Alzheimer's disease n = 16; Control n = 19) repeatedly indicated the location of a proprioceptive target - the hand- across mediolateral positions with or without vision. We measured bias and uncertainty locating the hand based on directional and variable error. We analysed errors using mixed-effects linear regression models and subsequently modelled observed errors as the product of proprioceptive and visual signals regarding hand location. With vision of the hand, its location was biased leftwards when indicating left hand position, with posterior cortical atrophy group biases being nearly doubled relative to controls (Estimated mean bias [95%CI]; Control:-15mm [-20, -10]; posterior cortical atrophy:-28mm [-46, -11]). Without vision, leftwards biases were particularly exaggerated in the tAD group (Control:-20mm [-25, -12]; typical Alzheimer's disease:-33mm [-39, -26]), with the posterior cortical atrophy group additionally exhibiting biases towards the body midline. Nearly half of patient participants (n = 19/41) exhibited abnormal biases relative to controls. Modelling attributed biases to elevated proprioceptive uncertainty or concurrent proprioceptive-visual uncertainty in typical Alzheimer's disease or posterior cortical atrophy groups. Perceived body position is disrupted in Alzheimer's disease clinical phenotypes, being both imprecise and biased towards 'local' body- and eye-centred references. Findings carry implications for assessment and management of spatial disorientation and misreaching following posterior cortical damage.

title: Association between early serum sodium variability and in-hospital mortality among adult intensive care unit admissions recorded in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database.
journal: The Journal of international medical research
abstract: ObjectiveSerum sodium abnormalities are common among critically ill patients; however, static measurements may not capture early fluctuations. This study evaluated the association between serum sodium variability measured within the first 48 h after intensive care unit admission and in-hospital mortality among adult intensive care unit admissions.MethodsThis retrospective observational cohort study used data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (version 3.1); we included the data of 41,165 adult first intensive care unit admissions for whom at least three serum sodium measurements taken within the first 48 h after intensive care unit admission were available. Sodium variability defined as the SD of sodium measurements within the specified observation window. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, selected comorbidities, mean sodium concentration, and electrolyte measurement count. Robustness analyses used a first 24 h window, excluded SD values ≥10 mmol/L, removed exact duplicate laboratory rows, tested nonlinearity with a natural cubic spline, and performed bootstrap internal validation.ResultsThe overall in-hospital mortality rate was 12.0% (4952/41,165). The mortality rates were 10.1%, 11.5%, 11.3%, and 15.2% across increasing quartiles 1-4, respectively, of sodium variability. Each 1 mmol/L increase in the SD of sodium concentrations was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital death (odds ratio: 1.14; 95% confidence interval, 1.12-1.17; p < 0.001). The association persisted during a 24 h window (odds ratio: 1.12; 95% confidence interval, 1.10-1.15) and among admissions with mean sodium concentrations of 135-145 mmol/L (odds ratio: 1.14; 95% confidence interval, 1.11-1.18). Spline modeling supported a nonlinear association (p < 0.001). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.765.ConclusionsGreater early serum sodium variability was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality. The retrospective design, selection of patients with repeated testing, and incomplete adjustment for acute illness severity and treatment preclude causal or clinical-use claims.

title: Spatial transcriptional signatures linked to brain activity patterns in MECP2 transgenic monkeys and human autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: Imaging transcriptomics studies in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have identified relevant biological pathways, yet the specific laminar molecular signatures associated with functional abnormalities remain largely unexplored. We integrated resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data from methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MECP2) transgenic monkeys-a model exhibiting autism-like behavior-with spatially resolved transcriptomic data to investigate layer-specific transcriptional signatures associated with altered brain activity. To evaluate their clinical relevance, we further projected these signatures onto human brain-wide gene expression data and examined their correlations with imaging alterations in ASD patients. Comparing to wild-type monkeys, MECP2 monkeys exhibited reduced brain activity in the prefrontal cortex and increased activity in the somatosensory cortices. These alterations were linked to expression profiles of two gene sets: one preferentially expressed in layers 2 and 6, primarily enriched in synaptic signaling; the other predominantly expressed in layer 3, primarily enriched in mitochondrial function. Additionally, two parvalbumin (PV) neuron subtypes showed opposing associations with alteration pattern: one concentrated in layer 5 of the prefrontal cortex; the other abundant in layers 3 and 4 of the somatosensory cortex. Projecting these transcriptional signatures onto human gene expression data revealed significant correlations with functional alterations in a subgroup of ASD patients. Our findings reveal layer-specific and cell-type-specific molecular signatures of MECP2-related brain dysfunction, offering insights into the biological basis of ASD and enhancing translational relevance across species.

title: Gut microbiota GABA regulation by intestinal pH, osmolality, and microbial consumption.
abstract: The production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by the gut microbiota has garnered attention due to its potential role as a driver of gut-brain axis signaling. However, mechanisms regulating microbiota-derived GABA under physiological conditions remain unclear. Here, we identified low pH and high osmolality as promoters of GABA production in the gut microbe Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by driving changes in the expression of the glutamate decarboxylase system. pH also emerged as a critical factor for enhancing GABA production in a broader set of gut microbes. However, in the cecal microbiota of specific pathogen-free mice and in an ex vivo model of the human colon microbiota, GABA levels did not increase under physiologically relevant acidic conditions. This can partly be explained by microbial GABA consumption. Consistently, reducing cecal pH increased GABA levels in Oligo-MM12 mice, a gnotobiotic model lacking GABA-consuming gut microbes. Our findings highlight the intricate balance between gut microbial GABA production, consumption, and environmental factors such as pH and osmolality.

title: Corrigendum to "A multispecies probiotic accelerates fear extinction and inhibits relapse in mice: Role of microglia" [Neuropharmacology, 193, (2021), 108613].
Therapeutic efficacy and auditory function of 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin with degrees of substitution beyond the pharmacopeial range in Niemann-Pick disease type C.
abstract: Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) is a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by impaired intracellular cholesterol trafficking and progressive neurodegeneration that ultimately leads to premature death. A cholesterol-solubilizing agent, 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD), is currently under clinical investigation for treating NPC, but its ototoxicity remains problematic. HP-β-CD is a mixture with varying degrees of substitution (DS) of 2-hydroxypropyl groups. However, investigations have been limited to the DS range specified in the European and United States Pharmacopoeias, and the impact of exceeding this range in NPC treatment is unknown. Here, using five HP-β-CDs with DS values of 4.6, 8.4, 9.9 (within the pharmacopeial range), 13.7, and 16.7 (exceeding this range), we evaluated their therapeutic efficacy in Npc1-deficient mice and toxicity in wild-type mice, following their intracerebroventricular injection. At the therapeutic dose, all HP-β-CDs significantly improved the lifespan and disease phenotype of Npc1-deficient mice, regardless of the DS value; however, these effects diminished for DS exceeding the pharmacopeial range. Auditory brainstem response indicated a significant elevation in hearing thresholds for all HP-β-CDs administered, regardless of DS values, even when the dose was reduced to half the therapeutic dose. These findings support prioritizing HP-β-CDs with DS values within, rather than beyond, the pharmacopeial range for clinical development.

title: Electric Stimulation for Tinnitus: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
abstract: Electric stimulation can suppress tinnitus, but efficacy depends on stimulation site, waveform, and patient-specific mechanisms. This review updates our 2015 point-of-attack framework with evidence from the past decade, spanning transcranial, ear-level, promontory and round-window, intracochlear, bimodal, vagus and cervical nerve, and invasive central stimulation. Randomized trials and FDA De Novo authorization of a sound-plus-tongue device have established the first clinically available noninvasive option, while prospective cochlear-implant data show large, durable tinnitus reduction comparable to other state-of-the-art treatments. Atraumatic, always-on implants may extend cochlear stimulation to patients with residual hearing. The central challenge remains matching stimulation to individual mechanisms.

title: Sleep problems and reduced mental well-being in adults with diabetic peripheral neuropathy and leg pain.
abstract: This study examined the associations between the presence of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), DPN with leg pain, sleep problems, and mental well-being. This is an observational cross-sectional study of adults with diabetes seen in an outpatient clinic between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025. Participants were invited to complete the Diaprofil questionnaire assessing sleep problems and mental wellbeing. DPN was defined based on vibration perception threshold, while DPN with leg pain was defined as the presence of DPN and self-reported leg pain. Associations were assessed using logistic regression (odds ratios [ORs]) and linear regression (β coefficients). Models were adjusted for age, gender, diabetes type and body mass index. A total of 3253 (74%) participants answered the questionnaire, with 1174 (36%) reporting sleep problems. Regression analyses were restricted to participants with complete DPN assessments (n = 654). DPN with leg pain was associated with twice the odds of sleep problems (Adjusted OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.30-3.15) and reduced mental well-being (Adjusted β -9.03, 95% CI -13.52 to -4.53), while the presence of DPN itself was not. DPN with leg pain-but not DPN alone-was independently associated with sleep problems and reduced mental well-being.

title: Cardiometabolic biomarker profiles across age groups during second-generation antipsychotic treatment: the RISKMet study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) develops along a cardiometabolic continuum that may not be fully captured by categorical definitions. We compared biomarker patterns in pediatric and adult patients treated with second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) and evaluated RISKMet-Bio, an exploratory composite measure of metabolic dysfunction. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 101 adults and 49 pediatric patients. Adults were classified using harmonized ATP III MetS criteria; pediatric metabolic dysfunction (MD) required central obesity plus one additional age-appropriate abnormality. MetS/MD was associated with higher insulin, C-peptide, leptin, and zonulin in both groups, with additional HbA1c and adiponectin alterations in adults. Most differences were attenuated after BMI adjustment. Increasing metabolic burden was associated with insulin-related biomarkers, leptin, and zonulin in both groups and with HbA1c and adiponectin only in adults. No age-group interaction remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. RISKMet-Bio discriminated MetS/MD with an apparent AUC of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.76-0.90), a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.80, and a repeated cross-validated AUC of 0.79. Eight adults and one pediatric participant without MetS/MD had upper-tertile values. SGA-treated patients showed an overlapping adiposity-related biomarker core and, descriptively, broader metabolic involvement in adults. RISKMet-Bio summarized biomarker heterogeneity but showed no clear incremental discrimination beyond anthropometric measures. Prospective external validation is required to assess the prediction of incident cardiometabolic outcomes.

title: Corrigendum to "Reward reactivity as a buffer against negative mental health consequences of pandemic-related stress: a preregistered analysis in the human connectome project in development" [Neuroimage 325 (2026) 121672].
Themes in sex chromosome drive and suppression in Drosophila and mice.
abstract: Biased transmission of alleles/chromosomes violates Mendelian segregation and is one of the most striking examples of intragenomic conflict. In both Drosophila and mice, sex chromosome drive thwarts equal segregation of sex chromosomes, often resulting in sex ratio distortion and/or sterility. Despite the vast evolutionary divergence between these taxa, sex chromosome drivers exhibit remarkable parallels. These include (i) recurrent emergence of multicopy drive loci, (ii) signatures of rapid evolutionary divergence in drivers, and (iii) the evolution of suppression. In this review, we synthesize the current understanding of sex chromosome drive and its suppression strategies in Drosophila and mice. By contrasting the drivers that orchestrate conflicts in these taxa, we uncover conserved themes and unique strategies in the evolution and suppression of sex chromosome drive.

title: Nonconvulsive status epilepticus: Is coma the phenotype that matters?
When is acute Epstein-Barr virus infection actually acute?
Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for cognitive rehabilitation.
abstract: This chapter describes a neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) approach to cognitive rehabilitation (CR) following acquired brain injury (ABI), with primary emphasis on traumatic brain injury and stroke. NIPE is conceptualised as more than information provision: neuroscience-informed explanations are used to help patients and families understand cognitive difficulties, recovery, rehabilitation strategies, and their implications for everyday functioning. Neuropsychological feedback is presented as a common context for NIPE, with attention to tailoring, functional translation, multimodal support, and verification of understanding. A dual-lens framework is proposed for NIPE delivery in CR. The therapeutic lens emphasises alliance, empathy and warmth, person-centred collaboration, shared explanatory models, and goal setting. The cognition-informed lens addresses how cognitive difficulties may affect learning through adjustment of information load and pacing, repetition, clear and concrete language, integration with existing knowledge, teach-back, and multimodal delivery. Together, these lenses inform considerations of timing and context and seven structural principles of NIPE: trustworthiness, interaction, salience, motivation, intensity, repetition, and multimodal/multimedia delivery. The chapter also considers NIPE content related to neuroplasticity, prognosis and recovery, rehabilitation approaches, and factors that may influence functioning and participation. Throughout, emphasis is placed on distinguishing established evidence from plausible but untested mechanisms and on presenting recovery in probabilistic rather than deterministic terms.

title: Developmental changes in the intestinal barrier, intestinal stem cells, enteric glial cells, intestinal microbiota and intestinal metabolites of weaned piglets.
journal: Animal nutrition (Zhongguo xu mu shou yi xue hui)
abstract: Weaning stress induces post-weaning diarrhea, which is linked to intestinal barrier dysfunction, immune disorders, enteric nervous system impairment, and altered gut microbiota composition and function. This study investigated the dynamic changes in intestinal barrier function, intestinal stem cells (ISC), enteric glial cells (EGC), gut microbiota, and metabolites in piglets during post-weaning. Forty-eight 21-d-old weaned Duroc × Landrace × Yorkshire piglets (6.81 ± 0.13 kg, six groups, each group had eight replicates and one piglet per replicate) were slaughtered for sampling at post-weaning d 0 (pre-weaning), 1, 4, 7, 11, and 14. Results showed that compared with d 0, the villus-to-crypt ratio (VCR) in the jejunum and ileum significantly decreased on post-weaning (P < 0.05). Moreover, the protein expression level MUC2 in the jejunum and ileum, the mRNA expression levels of β-catenin in the jejunum, LGR5, MUC2, GFAP, and S100β in the ileum significantly increased on post-weaning d 1 but β-catenin in the ileum significantly downregulated on post-weaning d 11 and 14 (P < 0.05). Additionally, the mRNA expression level of c-FOS in the ileum and the protein expression level of GFAP and S100β in the intestine significantly increased on post-weaning compared with pre-weaning (P < 0.05). Immunofluorescence results showed the expression of GFAP in the ileum significantly increased on post-weaning d 1 and 4 (P < 0.05) and returned to preweaning levels on post-weaning d 7. Furthermore, compared with d 0, colonic Chao1 and observed features indices significantly increased on post-weaning d 4, but decreased on d 11 and 14 post-weaning (P < 0.05). In addition, dominance index significantly increased, while Shannon and Simpson indices decreased on post-weaning d 11 and 14 than on post-weaning d 0 (P < 0.05). Moreover, acetate and propionate contents in colonic contents significantly increased, while isobutyrate and isovalerate contents decreased on post-weaning compared with pre-weaning (P < 0.05). Metabolomics revealed the differential metabolites significantly enriched in signaling pathways related to amino acid metabolism, immunity, and neurobiology. In conclusion, weaning stress induces injury of the intestinal barrier functions in piglets, activates intestinal stem cells and enteric glial cells, and significantly alters the composition and diversity of the intestinal microbiota and metabolites.

title: Unlocking neuronal plasticity: HDAC3 as a proposed epigenetic checkpoint.
abstract: Neuronal plasticity allows the nervous system to adapt to experience, environmental change, and injury through coordinated transcriptional, chromatin, synaptic, and circuit-level responses. HDAC3 is a context-dependent transcriptional regulator and an established molecular brake on selected neuronal and memory-related processes. What remains unresolved is whether the duration of HDAC3-associated dysregulation influences neuronal recovery once the dysregulated variable has been normalized. This Hypothesis and Theory article integrates evidence from epigenetics, molecular neuroscience, synaptic biology, and circuit neuroscience. The central model is designed for prospective testing by comparing otherwise matched HDAC3-associated perturbations of prespecified durations, verifying normalization in the relevant cell population, and assessing recovery at equivalent post-normalization intervals. Epigenomic, transcriptomic, synaptic, circuit, and behavioral measurements are proposed as complementary readouts rather than interchangeable evidence of causality. The model predicts that shorter and longer periods of HDAC3-associated dysregulation may be followed by different recovery trajectories. A shorter disturbance could leave transcriptional flexibility reduced yet recoverable, whereas a longer disturbance could be associated with more persistent chromatin and functional changes. These possibilities remain unproven. A reproducible duration-recovery relationship that survives control for initial dysfunction, cumulative injury, cell survival, exposure, and incomplete normalization would support the hypothesis. Comparable recovery across durations, non-replication, or effects attributable to those alternative explanations would weaken it. A duration effect alone would not establish a discrete checkpoint, biological irreversibility, or a therapeutic window. The framework extends the established molecular-brake concept rather than replacing it. Its contribution is a testable question about whether the history and duration of HDAC3-associated dysregulation influence subsequent neuronal recoverability. Therapeutic timing is therefore a motivation for experimental study, not an established clinical principle.

title: Differential effects of new allosteric modulators of HCN channel function on intrinsic excitability in CA1 pyramidal neurons.
abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are key regulators of neuronal excitability, with the HCN1 isoform deemed an especially promising therapeutic target for neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. However, currently available HCN modulators are limited by poor brain penetration, insufficient isoform selectivity and off-target effects. Here, we performed a comparative characterization of recently developed HCN-targeting small molecule drugs and biologic tools in native hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons ex vivo and heterologously expressed HCN1 channels in vitro, to determine how distinct mechanisms of HCN modulation influence neuronal excitability. Two new high-potency drug inhibitors, Org-2D and J&J12e, reduced the HCN-mediated current, I h , in neurons at nanomolar concentrations, causing changes in resting membrane potential, input resistance, rheobase and firing while preserving action potential waveform. Despite these similar effects, the two compounds differentially altered voltage sag and rebound depolarization, consistent with distinct allosteric mechanisms revealed by testing in vitro. In contrast, the HCN1-selective RO-275 compound showed limited efficacy in neurons, an effect potentially explained by its strong preference for binding to the closed state of HCN1 channels. Finally, the nanobody activator NB6 induced opposite effects on HCN-dependent membrane properties, showing that extracellular targeting can effectively enhance channel activity ex vivo. These findings show that the mechanism of HCN modulation critically determines the physiological effects of HCN-targeting compounds while highlighting both the promise and current limitations of small-molecule and biologic approaches for selectively targeting HCN channels in the brain.

title: Impact of hormonal changes on functional neurological disorder: an international online survey.
abstract: Functional neurological disorder (FND) affects women approximately three times more often than men. This disparity has largely been attributed to higher trauma prevalence and diagnostic bias while the potential contribution of hormonal influences has received little attention. An online questionnaire was distributed through FND clinics in 13 countries, assessing self-reported symptom change across five hormonal events: hormonal contraception, pregnancy, the menstrual cycle, menopause and gender-affirming hormone therapy.
