Eligible participants were cisgender women with a diagnosis of FND or gender minority individuals (transgender or non-binary). Perceived symptom change was rated on a 5-point scale ranging from large improvement to large worsening. Among 262 respondents (96% female; mean age 39 years), several hormonal contexts were associated with self-reported symptom changes. Overall, hormonal contraception and pregnancy were frequently associated with worsening of motor and cognitive symptoms and menopause with worsening across all symptom domains. Menstrual cycle analysis revealed a phase-dependent pattern: worsening was most frequently reported during menstruation and the luteal phase whereas improvement was most frequent during the follicular phase. Reported changes were not uniform, with a substantial proportion of participants describing no change or improvement. Self-reported FND symptom severity appears to vary with hormonal context, with motor and cognitive symptoms most consistently affected. Given the retrospective, self-report design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective research into the role of hormonal transitions in FND.

title: Multineuron whole-cell patch-clamp dataset of layer 5 pyramidal cell synaptic connectivity in juvenile rat somatosensory cortex.
abstract: Reconstructing the wiring rules of the neocortical microcircuit ideally requires simultaneous electrophysiological access to many neighboring neurons together with a precise record of the stimuli that probe their connections. This dataset extends the whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from Perin, Berger, and Markram (2011, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America [PNAS]), in which synaptic connectivity was mapped within local groups of thick-tufted layer 5 pyramidal neurons in the juvenile rat somatosensory cortex. It comprises 47 recording sessions, stored as Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) HDF5 files, in which up to 12 neurons were patched and recorded simultaneously in current-clamp mode using a purpose-built multineuron ("12-patch") setup. Across these sessions, the dataset includes 150,121 membrane-voltage acquisition sweeps (CurrentClampSeries; each a 5,000-20,000-sample waveform sampled at 5-10 kHz), 68,968 injected-current stimulus series (CurrentClampStimulusSeries-recorded on the secondary channel where available, otherwise reconstructed from the Igor wave-note protocol definitions), delivered under 160 distinct stimulus protocols, and 482 patched-cell electrode configurations. To make the collection queryable and artificial intelligence (AI)-ready without opening every HDF5 file, four analytical index tables are provided in Apache Parquet format-session_metadata (47 rows), acquisition_series (150,121 rows), electrode_metadata (482 rows) and stimulus_series (68,968 rows)-joined on session_id and the source NWB file path. The package is distributed as a FAIR² data product with machine-readable metadata in MLCommons Croissant format, World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) PROV Ontology (PROV-O) provenance, a full data dictionary and reproducible extraction scripts, under an Open Data Commons (ODC)-By version 1.0 attribution license. It offers a large, standardized, connectivity-oriented electrophysiology resource for microcircuit modeling, synaptic physiology methods development, and machine-learning applications on raw intracellular signals.

title: Conessine ameliorates anxiety and depression-like behaviors in reserpine-induced zebrafish (Danio rerio) through modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and BDNF signaling: experimental and computational evidence.
abstract: Depression and anxiety are common neuropsychiatric disorders associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and impaired neuroplasticity. Conessine, a plant-derived steroidal alkaloid with reported antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, has not been sufficiently investigated for its effects on anxiety- and depression-like behaviours. The current study investigated the effects of conessine in a reserpine-induced zebrafish model using behavioural, biochemical, molecular, histopathological, and computational approaches. Adult zebrafish were exposed to reserpine and subsequently treated with different concentrations of conessine. Behavioural responses were assessed using the Novel Tank Test and Light-Dark Test, while oxidative stress markers, monoamine oxidase (MAO) activity, brain histopathology, and the expression of TNF-α, IL-1β, and BDNF were evaluated. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the interaction of conessine with IKKβ. Conessine treatment increased exploratory behaviour and decreased freezing behaviour in reserpine-exposed zebrafish. It also increased antioxidant enzyme activity, decreased MAO activity, and improved histopathological alterations. Furthermore, conessine decreased the expression of TNF-α and IL-1β and increased BDNF expression. Computational analysis indicated favourable binding of conessine to IKKβ and a stable protein-ligand interaction during molecular dynamics simulation. Overall, conessine attenuated several behavioural, biochemical, inflammatory, and histopathological alterations associated with reserpine exposure. These findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of conessine.

title: Association Between Early-Onset Atopic Dermatitis and Risk of Asthma in Individuals With a Family History of Atopy: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Atopic diseases are immune-mediated allergic conditions characterized by hypersensitivity reactions following allergen exposure. The most common ones worldwide include atopic dermatitis (AD), asthma, and allergic rhinitis. AD, an inflammatory skin condition characterized by eczematous skin lesions, often appears as the first manifestation in the atopic march, which is the progression from AD to asthma and other allergic diseases. Our systematic review aims to assess the risk of asthma development in individuals with early-onset AD and a family history of atopy. We collected data from three databases, namely, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, and conducted a systematic review based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Initially, we identified 7,261 articles. After screening and quality assessment using various standardized tools, we included 12 high-quality studies in the final review. These comprised eight prospective cohort studies, two retrospective cohort studies, one narrative review, and one systematic review with meta-analysis. Our findings indicate that early-onset AD (within the first two years of life), especially when persistent or severe, significantly increases the risk of developing asthma during childhood. This risk is further amplified in individuals with a family history of atopic diseases. The review underscores early-onset AD and familial atopy as strong predictors of subsequent asthma development. Understanding the natural course of AD and its genetic and immunological links to other allergic conditions is crucial for early identification and preventive strategies.

title: Preoperative hypertonic sodium chloride hydroxyethyl starch infusion for delayed neurocognitive recovery in elderly hip fracture patients: a randomized controlled trial protocol.
abstract: Delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR) is a common neurological complication in elderly patients following hip fracture surgery and is associated with poor prognosis and reduced quality of life. Hypertonic sodium chloride hydroxyethyl starch (HSH) has both volume-expanding and immunomodulatory properties. Our previous animal studies demonstrated that HSH exerts neuroprotective effects by stabilizing the blood-brain barrier, with greater efficacy than hypertonic saline or hydroxyethyl starch alone. However, high-quality clinical evidence regarding its cognitive protective effect in elderly hip fracture patients is lacking. This trial aims to evaluate the preventive effect and mechanisms of preoperative prophylactic HSH infusion on dNCR in elderly patients with hip fracture. The findings are expected to provide high-quality evidence for optimizing perioperative fluid management strategies and offer a novel, practical approach for perioperative cognitive protection in this vulnerable population. This is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, superiority trial. A total of 148 elderly patients aged ≥65 years with ASA physical status I-III scheduled for hip fracture surgery will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the HSH group (4 ml/kg HSH40 infused 30 min before anesthesia induction) or the control group (equal volume of normal saline). The primary outcome is the incidence of dNCR at postoperative day 7, defined as a ≥2-point decrease in Montreal Cognitive Assessment score from baseline. Secondary outcomes include exploratory cognitive function at 1 and 3 months postoperatively assessed by the Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status-Modified, days alive and at home within 30 days postoperatively, quality of recovery assessed by the QoR-15 scale, serum biomarkers of blood-brain barrier injury and inflammation (S100β, MMP-9, IL-6), incidence of postoperative delirium, and postoperative complications. Safety indicators include electrolytes, coagulation function, and liver and kidney function. This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of Chongqing Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital (Ethics Approval No. 2025-KY-HY66). https://www.chictr.org.cn, identifier: ChiCTR2600122105.

title: Programmed cell death in dementia: advances in pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Dementia comprises a group of neurodegenerative disorders characterized primarily by progressive cognitive decline. Its central pathological feature is the irreversible loss of neurons, which leads to the continuous deterioration of memory, language, and executive functions. In recent years, programmed cell death (PCD), as a major form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention because of its critical involvement in neuronal loss during the development of dementia. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that multiple forms of PCD, including apoptosis, autophagic cell death, necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, are aberrantly activated in common dementia subtypes such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD), where they synergistically promote neurodegeneration through distinct molecular mechanisms. However, therapeutic interventions targeting a single PCD pathway are often insufficient to halt disease progression, and the pathological heterogeneity among different dementia subtypes further complicates treatment. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms and pathological contributions of the major forms of PCD in dementia and further discusses emerging therapeutic strategies targeting PCD pathways, including small-molecule inhibitors, genetic modulation, and nanomedicine-based drug delivery systems. By integrating recent advances in this field, this review aims to provide a theoretical framework and translational perspectives for the development of early diagnostic biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies for dementia.

title: Effect of Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine) on Symptoms and Quality of Life in Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS): A Randomized, Double-Blinded Clinical Trial.
journal: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel movements. Vitamin B6 has been proposed to influence gastrointestinal function through effects on neurotransmitter activity, gut microbiota, and inflammation. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin B6 supplementation on symptom severity and quality of life in patients with IBS. This randomized, double-blinded clinical trial was conducted on 60 patients with IBS at a gastroenterology clinic in Mashhad, Iran. Participants were stratified by IBS subtype and randomly assigned to receive either vitamin B6 or a placebo for 4 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in IBS symptom severity scoring system (IBS-SSS), and the secondary outcome was quality of life assessed using the IBS-QoL questionnaire. Assessments were performed at baseline and at the end of the intervention period. No significant differences were observed between the vitamin B6 and placebo groups in changes in IBS-SSS or IBS-QoL scores. Subgroup analysis revealed within-group improvements in patients with constipation-predominant IBS (IBS-C) and mixed-type IBS (IBS-M) (p = 0.004 and p = 0.005, respectively). Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) demonstrated that baseline IBS symptom severity was the strongest predictor of posttreatment outcomes, while neither treatment allocation nor IBS subtype independently influenced outcomes. Vitamin B6 supplementation did not significantly improve overall IBS outcomes compared with placebo. Further large-scale randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up periods are needed to confirm these findings and clarify underlying mechanisms.

title: Bayesian reappraisal of favorable anti-amyloid trials in Alzheimer's disease: updating the cumulative evidence.
abstract: Recent favorable trials of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies have renewed interest in disease-modifying therapies for Alzheimer's disease. However, statistically significant findings from individual trials do not necessarily establish clinically meaningful benefit when interpreted in the context of the existing body of evidence. A cumulative assessment is therefore needed to distinguish evidence for a measurable treatment effect from evidence that its magnitude is clinically important. We applied Bayesian updating to integrate evidence from recent favorable anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody trials with prior evidence synthesized from a Cochrane systematic review. Posterior distributions were estimated for changes in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB), Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale, Mini-Mental State Examination, and amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema (ARIA-E). Posterior probabilities were calculated across clinically relevant efficacy and safety thresholds, allowing direct estimation of the probability of any treatment benefit, clinically meaningful benefit, and treatment-related harm. Posterior estimates indicated a high probability that anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody treatment results in a measurable slowing of cognitive decline relative to placebo. For CDR-SB, the posterior probability of any benefit was high, whereas the probability of reaching increasingly stringent thresholds of clinical relevance declined sharply and the probability of achieving the minimal clinically important difference remained very low. Secondary cognitive outcomes showed a similar pattern. In contrast, Bayesian updating indicated near-certain evidence of increased ARIA-E risk, with posterior estimates corresponding to an approximately 10-fold increase relative to placebo. Bayesian updating distinguishes evidence supporting the existence of a treatment effect from evidence supporting clinically meaningful benefit. Integrating favorable trials with accumulated evidence suggests that anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies produce modest average slowing of cognitive decline while maintaining substantial treatment-related risks. Longer-term randomized and open-label follow-up remains important for determining whether these modest differences persist, increase, or diminish over time.

title: Stress granule assembly is a trigger for tumor necrosis factor alpha production in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells.
abstract: Tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) is a key pro-inflammatory cytokine that orchestrates innate immune responses to infections and other cellular stressors. Chronic inflammation causes persistent TNF-α overproduction, which promotes apoptosis and necroptosis. Excessive production of TNF-α contributes to neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and multiple sclerosis. Although anti-TNF-α antibodies are effective in treating autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, they cannot penetrate the brain and reduce TNF-α levels in neuronal cells. Here, we investigate the role of stress granule formation in regulating TNF-α production in human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Stress granules are dynamic membraneless ribonucleoprotein complexes that assemble in response to various stress stimuli. They contain RNAs, RNA-binding proteins, and ribosomal components. In particular, the RNA-binding proteins TIA-1, TIAR, and FXR1, which negatively regulate TNF mRNA translation, are incorporated into stress granules under stress. Using immunocytochemistry, we show that FXR1 is progressively recruited to stress granules during sodium arsenite-induced stress in SH-SY5Y cells. Sequestration of FXR1 into stress granules disrupts its interaction with TNF mRNA, resulting in increased TNF-α production. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of stress granule assembly by the integrated stress response inhibitor (ISRIB) prevents stress-induced excessive TNF-α production in SH-SY5Y cells. Thus, our findings indicate that stress granule assembly triggers TNF-α production. Given that some known stress granule inhibitors can cross the blood-brain barrier, we propose that they may be promising agents for reducing the excessive neurotoxic production of TNF-α during neuroinflammation, provided that our findings are confirmed in other cell cultures and in vivo.

title: The Neurosequential Model in Education: an Aotearoa New Zealand Story.
abstract: Trauma informed education is an emerging paradigm which is based on neuroscientific understandings that centre relational safety and connection. The Neurosequential Model in Education is one such trauma-informed approach involving the children, school staff, families, and the wider community. This paper presents a descriptive case study of a small primary school in Aotearoa New Zealand in which this approach was implemented. The case study explores the question "What were the experiences of staff in an Aotearoa New Zealand primary school who took part in the implementation of the Neurosequential Model in Education?" The participants' stories are inspiring, hopeful and transformative. Findings show participants increased their knowledge and understanding of how the brain works, experienced their own healing, developed a greater capacity to self-regulate and co-regulate, and built a strong therapeutic web for the students with the effects beginning to flow out to parents and whānau. Moreover, a unique model was created through weaving together the neuroscience of the Neurosequential Model in Education and the indigenous wisdom of Te Ao Māori. This descriptive case study makes a unique contribution to this developing field of research and can serve as one exemplar of how the approach can be implemented.

title: Postcentral cortical thickness reduction in trigeminal neuralgia: a whole-brain surface-based morphometry MRI study.
abstract: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a neuropathic pain disorder characterized by paroxysmal unilateral facial pain evoked by innocuous cutaneous stimulation or manoeuvres. In classical and idiopathic TN, objective evidence of somatosensory system damage is often difficult to demonstrate. Neuroimaging studies suggest cortical structural alterations, though findings have been inconsistent, likely reflecting variability in case definitions and cortical measurement methodologies. We therefore investigated cortical thickness changes in a biologically homogeneous cohort of patients with right-sided TN using a whole-brain surface-based morphometry (SBM) approach. 60 patients with classical or idiopathic right-sided TN and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent 3 T structural MRI. Cortical thickness was computed using FreeSurfer. Whole-brain vertex-wise group comparisons were performed using a General Linear Model (GLM) with a non-parametric permutation-based cluster-wise correction for multiple comparisons. Compared with controls, patients with TN showed significantly reduced cortical thickness in eight clusters. The largest and most significant cluster was located in the left postcentral gyrus. Additional clusters were identified in the bilateral insular-temporal regions, the right precentral-postcentral region, the right lateral occipital cortex, and the right parieto-occipital junction. Cortical thickness within significant clusters did not correlate with disease duration. Right-sided TN is associated with focal cortical thinning involving both somatosensory and associative cortical regions. While involvement of insular, parietal, and occipital cortices is consistent with network-level structural reorganization observed in chronic pain conditions, thinning of the contralateral postcentral cortex may reflect central changes secondary to damage of primary trigeminal afferents.

title: Environmental neurotoxicity in early life: nodding syndrome as a model of neurodevelopmental priming and neurodegenerative vulnerability.
abstract: Nodding syndrome (NS) is a childhood-onset epileptic disorder reported in sub-Saharan Africa, characterized by seizures, developmental delay, progressive neurological decline, and tau pathology. Its rapid clinical progression provides an opportunity to investigate how early developmental vulnerability may intersect with neurodegenerative processes. We reanalyzed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic data from Ugandan patients with NS (n = 9) and age-comparable controls (n = 9) to identify molecular signatures associated with this convergence. Differential protein abundance implicated proteostasis, bioenergetics, genomic and epigenetic regulation, and structural and neurovascular integrity. Reduced abundance of PP1/PP2A-associated components and V-ATPase subunits, together with increased lysosomal hydrolases, suggested disturbances in phosphoregulatory and lysosomal homeostasis. Changes in developmental and cytoskeletal proteins further implicated neuronal maturation and structural stability. These signatures showed molecular parallels with MECP2-related disorders and lysosomal tauopathies, without implying a shared etiology. Collectively, the findings support a testable model in which compromised metabolic and proteostatic resilience may link developmental vulnerability to progressive neurological dysfunction. Malnutrition, infections, and regionally relevant environmental biotoxins may contribute to this convergence, although their involvement was not directly assessed. Despite the small cohort and the inferential limits of CSF proteomics, this study provides a molecular basis for investigating the neurodevelopmental-neurodegenerative continuum in NS and testing whether early molecular signatures can predict disease trajectories. The model prioritizes homeostatic resilience as a potential determinant of neurological health and a target for future preventive research.

title: Human blood-brain barrier models for intracerebral hemorrhage: From conventional in vitro systems to advanced microphysiological platforms.
abstract: Intracerebral bleeding (ICH), the deadliest type of bleeding stroke, has always been a significant source of death and neurological disability all around the world. Despite extensive laboratory research, translating trial therapies into real-world practice has been limited because current animal models are often not clinically relevant. At the same time, it is widely recognized that there is a strong need for newly developed blood-brain barrier models. Recent breakthroughs in tissue engineering, stem cell theory, materials science, and microfabrication have enabled the creation of new blood-brain barrier models. These include moist and dry Transwell-based co-culture models, three-dimensional hydrogel-supported models, human pluripotent stem cell-based models, multicellular spheroids and organoids, and microfluidic blood-brain barrier devices and organoids that can operate under perfusion conditions. Each new model offers clear advantages for blood-brain barrier research, but also has serious disadvantages. This review critically analyses current in vitro human BBB models in the context of ICH pathophysiology and explains their formulations, translational applications, advantages, and disadvantages. It also describes new tools that use biomaterials, vascularisation, and dynamic perfusion to improve model fidelity. Hence, new-generation human BBB model platforms may pave the way for replacing animal models in explaining disease mechanisms, developing therapies, and improving precision medicine for ICH.

title: Preclinical medical students with stronger psychological capital report more motivated learning strategies: a cross-sectional study in Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Medical education places considerable academic and psychological demands on students, and positive psychological resources may help them sustain effective learning. Psychological capital (PsyCap) comprises hope, efficacy, resilience, and optimism; however, how its dimensions relate to motivated learning strategies among medical students remains underexplored, particularly in Saudi Arabia. This cross-sectional study examined these associations among 376 of 400 invited preclinical (Years 1-3) medical students (response rate 94.0%) at King Faisal University, Al-Hasa, Saudi Arabia, who completed the 12-item Psychological Capital Questionnaire (PCQ-12) and a 32-item version of the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ) adapted for medical students. Measurement models were examined with confirmatory factor analysis. Associations were tested with Pearson correlations (Holm-adjusted) and hierarchical multiple linear regression adjusted for age, gender, year of study, and grade point average (GPA), and dominance analysis was used to compare the relative contributions of the PsyCap dimensions. All PsyCap dimensions were positively correlated with all MSLQ domains (r = 0.33-0.55). Beyond the covariates, the PsyCap dimensions explained an additional 35.3% of the variance in overall motivated learning strategies (ΔR² = 0.353, p < 0.001). Optimism (β = 0.25), hope (β = 0.22), and efficacy (β = 0.15) were independently associated with motivated learning strategies, whereas resilience was not (β = 0.09, p = 0.130). Resilience shared almost all of its explained variance with the other dimensions, its independent association became significant when influential observations were excluded, and, for overall motivated learning strategies, its contribution was not significantly smaller than those of the other dimensions. Higher psychological capital, particularly hope and optimism, was associated with greater use of motivated learning strategies among preclinical medical students. Because the study was cross-sectional and conducted at a single institution, the findings do not establish causality; PsyCap-based interventions warrant testing in longitudinal and experimental studies.

title: Peripheral T- and B-cell immune signatures in early Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Neuroinflammation and peripheral adaptive immune dysregulation have been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but whether peripheral immune alterations are detectable at the earliest biomarker-defined stages remains unclear. Most immunophenotyping studies enrolled patients with clinically manifest dementia without biomarker confirmation. We conducted a prospective, observational, single-centre study in consecutive adults with normal cognition or mild cognitive impairment (MMSE >22; CDR 0-0.5). Participants were classified by CSF and blood biomarkers into biomarker-defined AD, other dementias (OD), and non-degenerative cognitive complaints (NDC). Peripheral blood surface-marker immunophenotyping by multiparametric flow cytometry characterised B-cell and T-cell compartments, including regulatory, conventional helper, follicular helper, and double-negative T-cell subsets. Groups were compared using Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted parametric and non-parametric tests. Exploratory analyses included principal component analysis, permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA), correlations between immune subsets and AD biomarkers, and a logistic regression model discriminating AD from NDC, evaluated by ROC analysis. Seventy-nine participants were included (AD n=43, OD n=18, NDC n=18). No significant differences were detected in any lymphocyte population between biomarker-defined AD and NDC after multiple-testing correction. The clearest, albeit modest, multivariate separation was between AD and OD, driven by nominally higher frequencies of Th17-like regulatory T cells and Th9-like cells in OD that did not survive correction, except for Th17-like regulatory T cells in the age- and sex-adjusted AD-versus-OD comparison. Double-negative γδ T cells were numerically, but not significantly, lower in AD than in NDC, and an exploratory logistic model including double-negative T-cell subsets achieved moderate discrimination (AUC 0.743) without external validation. Correlations between immune subsets and AD biomarkers were weak; the most apparent was between Th17-like regulatory T cells and CSF neurofilament light chain, not amyloid-β or tau. No significant differences in peripheral adaptive immune profiles were detected between biomarker-defined early AD and NDC, suggesting that overt peripheral immune activation is not yet established at the earliest stages of the Alzheimer's continuum. The exploratory differences between AD and OD, involving Th17-like regulatory T cells and Th9-like cells, may reflect Treg plasticity and IL-9 axis activation in active neurodegeneration, warranting functional validation. These signatures should not be regarded as candidate biomarkers for early AD detection.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses explore potential mechanisms underlying the protective effects of Mailuoning oral liquid after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice.
abstract: Secondary brain injury driven by neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption contributes substantially to poor outcomes after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Mailuoning oral liquid (MLN) has anti-inflammatory and vascular-protective activities; however, its protective effects and mechanisms in ICH remain unknown. To evaluate the protective effects of MLN after ICH and explore the potential underlying mechanisms. A collagenase-induced ICH model was established in C57BL/6 J mice. Neurological deficits, brain injury, cerebral edema, BBB dysfunction, and BBB-related proteins were assessed. Transcriptomics and network pharmacology were integrated to identify candidate targets and pathways, followed by protein-level validation and phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) challenge. MLN improved neurological function, attenuated perihematomal injury and early hematoma burden, reduced cerebral edema and BBB leakage, increased claudin-5, occludin, and ZO-1, and decreased MMP-9. Transcriptomics identified 383 MLN-responsive genes enriched mainly in inflammatory and immune pathways, including NF-κB signaling. Network pharmacology independently identified 114 MLN-ICH targets and similarly highlighted inflammation-related pathways. Integrated analysis yielded 95 MLN-reversed ICH-responsive genes and three cross-supported candidates, F10, Ccl2, and Tnf. MLN reduced total NF-κB p65, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 protein expression, whereas PMA co-treatment partially attenuated MLN-associated improvements in neurological function and BBB-related protein expression. MLN alleviates secondary brain injury and preserves BBB integrity after ICH. These protective effects may be associated with the modulation of NF-κB-related inflammatory responses and MMP-9-associated BBB alterations.

title: Hallucinating Together: AI Chatbots in Psychedelic Therapy.
Chess-based cognitive remediation training and alcohol cue reactivity in alcohol use disorder: exploratory evidence for supplementary motor area activation changes.
abstract: Cue-induced craving is a key driver of relapse in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet standard inpatient treatments do not directly target the neurocognitive control deficits underlying it. Chess-based cognitive remediation training (CB-CRT) is a manualised group intervention engaging working memory, attention, and inhibitory control. This exploratory study examined whether CB-CRT modulates neural cue reactivity in AUD. In this study (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04057534), 41 abstinent inpatients with AUD were quasi-randomised to treatment as usual (TAU; n = 16) or TAU plus CB-CRT (n = 25) over 6 weeks at a rehabilitation center. Neural responses to alcohol-related cues were assessed with a validated cue reactivity paradigm before and after the intervention period (T1, T2); the primary endpoint was the change in BOLD activation (Alcohol > Rest). Craving (Obsessive Compulsive Drinking Scale, OCDS; Alcohol Urge Questionnaire, AUQ) and depressive symptoms (Beck Depression Inventory II, BDI) were assessed and correlated with neural changes. Whole-brain analysis revealed a significant Time × Group interaction in the supplementary motor area (SMA; peak MNI -2, 4, 80; k = 544; cluster-level pFWE = 0.025), with increased SMA activation in CB-CRT + TAU and a decrease in TAU. Within CB-CRT + TAU, change in SMA activation correlated positively with change in obsessive-compulsive craving (OCDS total: r = 0.439, p = 0.032; cognitive subscale: r = 0.453, p = 0.026). The CB-CRT + TAU showed significant within-group reductions in BDI and OCDS; the between-group comparison of change scores before baseline adjustment reached significance for BDI only (d = -0.80), which was no longer significant after adjustment. These exploratory findings indicate differential longitudinal SMA activation between groups during alcohol-cue viewing relative to rest. CB-CRT might have additional effect against depressive symptoms, though this finding was affected by baseline severity and requires further validation. ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT04057534.

title: Intervention-specific knowledge, attitudes, and practices among guardians of children with myopia: a multicity cross-sectional survey in China.
abstract: To compare guardians' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) across three commonly used myopia-management modalities and to identify associated sociodemographic factors. A multicity cross-sectional survey was conducted among guardians of children aged 6-12 years in eight Chinese cities using convenience and snowball sampling. The self-administered questionnaires assessed general myopia-related knowledge, awareness of the effects of interventions, and intervention-specific KAP regarding 0.01% atropine eye drops, spectacles, and orthokeratology. Exploratory psychometric properties were assessed, and generalized estimating equations (GEE), Spearman correlations, logistic regression, and bootstrap linear regression were applied. Among 1,509 valid questionnaires, 726 guardians reported having a child with myopia (48.1%). With multiple responses permitted, reported use was most frequent for spectacles (82.1%), followed by 0.01% atropine eye drops (15.8%) and orthokeratology (15.0%). Orthokeratology had the highest adjusted KAP scores (4.17, 3.98, and 4.23, respectively), followed by spectacles and 0.01% atropine. KAP domains were positively intercorrelated for both spectacles and orthokeratology. For 0.01% atropine, attitude and practice scores were negatively correlated (ρ = -0.538, p < 0.001) and no significant association was identified between knowledge and practice. Among guardians of spectacle users, practice scores were lower among those aged 19-34 years compared with those aged 35-49 years (B = -1.17, 95% CI: -1.74 to -0.58; p < 0.001; q = 0.024) and among those with less than a bachelor's degree (B = -0.79, 95% CI: -1.25 to -0.35; p = 0.001; q = 0.024). Guardians' KAP levels and inter-domain correlations differed across interventions. These findings may support intervention-specific education and balanced clinician-guardian communication.

title: Neural architecture of the jhānas: a gamma-infraslow duet with quantum overtones.
abstract: Building on previous electrophysiological investigations that posited meditative absorption (jhāna) as a radical disruption of sensory default consciousness (DCs), this study explores the underlying non-linear neural architectures and state transitions. Re-analysis of long-duration (n = 18) DC-stabilized records reveals that alpha spindles index three distinct developmental stages of the first jhāna, reflecting attentional mastery through vitakka (directed attention) and vicāra (sustained attention). A broadband (0.005-150 Hz) 3D eLoreta source analysis of a major 4,000 µV relaxation-oscillation (R-O) transition into the second jhāna, confirms the active silencing of fronto-temporal linguistic networks, leading to the profound mental stillness characteristic of higher absorption states. This macro state transition is driven by a near-absolute variance concentration of infraslow rhythms localized to the midline vertex (z = 70) supplementary motor area (SMA), supported by a lateralized left-hemisphere temporal and visual-gating gamma network. As the jhāna hierarchy deepens, the brain recruits an unprecedented electrophysiological dynamic range. Spanning four orders of magnitude in time (102-10-2 s) bridging the absolute physical boundaries of human neurobiology, this architecture couples high-amplitude infraslow carriers (2,000-4,000 µV) to ultra-fast gamma microbursts (100-200 µV). This coordinated gamma-infraslow duet constructs an impenetrable, low-entropy Markov blanket, actively insulating the internal cognitive field from sensory perturbation while maintaining waking alertness. Concurrently, the 600-fold deceleration of cortical rhythms at the vertex facilitates heightened synchrony with visceral neurovascular systems. At critical R-O inflection thresholds, brief (1-2 s) global high-gamma microbursts function as inhibitory sweeps across left-lateralized hubs (BA 47, BA 21/22/38), dismantling emerging inner speech to protect absorptive stability. The study further demonstrates that the jhāna hierarchy follows a scale-free trajectory distinct from the θ, α, β frequency bands of default sensory consciousness (DCs), bypassing the 1 Hz deep-sleep transition, replacing nested sensory Markov blankets with a singular global boundary at the fourth-jhāna limit-a system with intriguing similarities to noise-shielded quantum "superposition." We conclude that jhāna consciousness (JCs) constitutes an autonomous and previously unrecognized, highly structured second-tier of human consciousness, rather than an altered state of (sensory) consciousness (ASC).

title: Case Report: Postoperative central nervous system infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
abstract: Sulbactam-durlobactam in combination with a carbapenem is recommended as the preferred treatment for invasive carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections in the 2026 Infectious Diseases Society of America guidance. However, clinical experience with sulbactam-durlobactam for treating CRAB-induced central nervous system (CNS) infections remains extremely limited, and intraventricular/intrathecal polymyxins are still recommended as established therapy for CRAB ventriculitis/meningitis. We report two cases of CRAB-induced CNS meningitis/ventriculitis that occurred following cranial neurosurgery. Both patients presented with recurrent fever and altered mental status after brain surgery and showed an inadequate response to conventional antimicrobial regimens, including intravenous polymyxin B with intrathecal or intraventricular administration. After conversion to combination therapy of sulbactam-durlobactam and meropenem, along with neurosurgical intervention, both patients achieved fever control and sustained microbiological and laboratory improvement. These cases provide additional clinical evidence suggesting that, in patients with surgically disrupted blood-brain barriers, intravenous administration of sulbactam-durlobactam in combination with meropenem may represent an effective therapeutic option for CNS infections caused by CRAB. However, the applicability of this regimen may be limited to patients with blood-brain barrier impairment. Its use in this population still requires further pharmacokinetic validation.

title: Anisodamine hydrobromide exposure and recovery from sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Anisodamine hydrobromide has been used as an adjunctive therapy for circulatory shock and microcirculatory dysfunction; however, its association with recovery from sepsis-associated encephalopathy remains unclear. This study examined the relationship between anisodamine hydrobromide exposure and neurological recovery in patients with sepsis. This two-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients with sepsis admitted to two tertiary hospitals in China between January 2020 and May 2026. Patients who received anisodamine hydrobromide within 24 h of admission were compared with those who did not. The primary outcome was delirium/coma-free days within 7 days of admission. Secondary outcomes included new-onset delirium, delirium duration, time to Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) negativity, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score changes, lactate clearance, capillary refill time (CRT), endothelial injury biomarkers, blood-brain barrier and neural injury biomarkers, and safety outcomes. In total, 499 patients were included, of whom 226 received anisodamine hydrobromide and 273 were controls. Anisodamine hydrobromide exposure was associated with more delirium/coma-free days within 7 days than the control group, with negative binomial regression yielding consistent results. The incidence of new-onset delirium did not differ significantly between groups. Among patients who developed delirium, anisodamine hydrobromide exposure was associated with shorter delirium duration. It was also associated with earlier CAM-ICU negativity, greater GCS improvement, higher lactate clearance, shorter CRT, and greater reductions in soluble thrombomodulin, angiopoietin-2, S100β, neuron-specific enolase, and glial fibrillary acidic protein. Anticholinergic-related adverse events were not significantly increased in the anisodamine hydrobromide group. Anisodamine hydrobromide exposure was associated with more delirium/coma-free days, shorter delirium duration, earlier CAM-ICU negativity, and greater improvements in neurological, microcirculatory, endothelial, and blood-brain barrier/neural injury markers in patients with sepsis.

title: Stress Hyperglycemia Predicts Recurrent Stroke in Patients With Acute Mild Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA of Presumed Atherosclerotic Cause.
abstract: To evaluate the association between stress hyperglycemia and recurrent stroke among Chinese patients with acute mild ischemic stroke (IS) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA) caused by intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis. This study was a post hoc analysis of the INSPIRES (Intensive Statin and Antiplatelet Therapy for Acute High-Risk Intracranial or Extracranial Atherosclerosis) trial, which was a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial clinical trial. Stress hyperglycemia was characterized using two complementary measures, including the glycemic gap (GG) and the admission blood glucose-to-HbA1c (ABG/HbA1c ratio). The GG was calculated using ABG divided by (1.59 [mmol/L] × HbA1c [%] - 2.59). The principal efficacy endpoint was recurrent stroke within 90 days. Secondary endpoints mainly included composite vascular events, IS, and poor functional outcomes at 90 days. The primary safety endpoint was moderate-to-severe bleeding by 90 days. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate associations between stress hyperglycemia and recurrent stroke. Among 4515 patients, the median age was 65 years (IQR, 57-71 years), and 1621 (35.9%) were women. In fully adjusted analyses, the highest quartile of GG and the ABG/HbA1c ratio were associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke (HR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.09-2.08; HR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.10-2.16; all p for trend < 0.05). Comparable findings were observed for secondary efficacy endpoints. Neither GG nor the ABG/HbA1c ratio was statistically associated with safety endpoints. In this post hoc analysis, stress hyperglycemia was significantly associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke among Chinese patients with acute mild IS or high-risk TIA of presumed atherosclerotic cause. Further investigation is needed to validate this association and explore the underlying mechanisms.

title: No detectable choroid plexus enlargement in clinically premanifest Huntington's disease.
abstract: BackgroundHuntington's disease (HD) is a progressive autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene, producing an elongated polyglutamine tract in the huntingtin protein. The disease is characterized by motor dysfunction, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms, with early striatal neurodegeneration. HD is also associated with immune activation and neuroinflammation. The choroid plexus (ChP), a vascularized structure responsible for cerebrospinal fluid production and immune surveillance, is consistently enlarged across neurological and psychiatric disorders including Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and major depressive disorder. In these conditions, ChP enlargement correlates with inflammatory markers and disease severity, suggesting it may represent a common response to nervous system pathology. Recent evidence indicates that ChP volume is increased in manifest HD, but whether ChP volume is altered in premanifest HD remains unclear.MethodsThe choroid plexus was manually segmented on T1-weighted MRI scans from premanifest HD participants and healthy controls. ChP volume was compared between groups and correlated with the CAP-100 score as a measure of estimated disease burden.ResultsDespite significant atrophy of the caudate and putamen, ChP volume did not differ between groups (difference 26 mm3, 2.6% of mean volume; minimum detectable difference 271 mm3). ChP volume was not significantly associated with the CAP-100 score.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that choroid plexus enlargement does not accompany the early striatal volume loss observed in our premanifest HD cohort. While HD has been associated with immune activation, our results do not support choroid plexus enlargement as an early structural correlate of this process.

title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, not C-reactive protein, is associated with midlife cognition.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Systemic inflammation is implicated in Alzheimer's disease, but its role during preclinical stages and interaction with apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) remain unclear. We analyzed longitudinal serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in 441 cognitively healthy midlife adults from the PREVENT Dementia cohort, sampled 3 years apart. Cognition was assessed using the Addenbrooke Cognitive Examination III, adjusted for site, age, sex, education, and APOE ε4. A longitudinal increase in NLR, but not CRP, was associated with midlife cognitive decline (β = -0.763, p = 0.031), independent of APOE ε4. In exploratory analyses, APOE ε4 carriers had lower baseline CRP than non-carriers, a difference that attenuated over follow-up; NLR showed no such association. Rising NLR may be a more sensitive marker of early midlife cognitive change than CRP, suggesting it captures immune dysfunction beyond systemic inflammation.

title: NeuN as a Marker of Molecular Heterogeneity in the Spiral Ganglion of C57BL/6J Mice.
abstract: Spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) comprise molecularly distinct subtypes in several rodent and primate species. These subtypes can be differentiated using gene markers such as Calb2 (calretinin) for Ia/Ib, Pou4f1 (Brn3a) for Ic, and Prph (Peripherin) for Type II. How the levels of these markers vary at the protein level, and how such variation encodes subtype identity, has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that, in C57BL/6J mice, NeuN (Rbfox3), a widely used neuronal marker, exhibits a developmentally stable gradient that distinguishes all four subtypes. Using quantitative immunofluorescence at P14, 2 months, and 12 months, we show that NeuN expression is highest in Type Ic neurons, intermediate in Type Ib, low in Type Ia, and absent from Type II neurons. NeuN intensity is inversely correlated with calretinin and positively correlated with Brn3a, revealing coordinated, graded relationships rather than categorical on/off patterns. Quadruple‑labeling experiments confirm a correspondence between NeuN brightness tiers and subtype identity defined by calretinin/Brn3a combinations. Across the tonotopic axis, NeuN and calretinin display significant regional variation in young adults (2 months), whereas Brn3a remains spatially uniform. Developmental and aging analyses further show that NeuN and calretinin undergo location‑dependent modulation across the lifespan, while Brn3a remains stable. Despite age‑related auditory threshold elevations at 12 months, NeuN heterogeneity and its correlations with other markers are preserved. Together, these findings demonstrate that, in C57BL/6J mice, SGN subtype identity is associated with protein-level gradients and coordinated inter-marker relationships and identify NeuN as a novel tool with potential applications in basic research and pathological assessment of SGN diversity.

title: Histamine Clearance by Enteric Glial Histamine N-Methyltransferase (Hnmt) Shapes Enteric Neurocircuit Activity and Colonic Motor Function.
abstract: Histamine is an important neuromodulator that affects the activity of gut neurons that control intestinal motility and sensations. Elevated histamine levels contribute to mechanisms that drive gut pain and dysmotility in irritable bowel syndrome; yet mechanisms regulating histamine in gut neural networks are poorly understood. Here, we used an inducible, cell-specific ablation model, in vivo and in vitro motility assays, and cellular imaging of enteric neuron activity to study how deleting enteric glial histamine N-methyltransferase (Hnmt) affects gut motility through effects on enteric neuron signaling. In vivo assays showed that deleting glial Hnmt produced slower whole gut transit and rectal bead expulsion time. In vitro organ bath studies revealed that effects on colonic contractility were related to a decrease in neurogenic relaxations and to rhythmic, spontaneous colonic contractions in glial Hnmt knockouts. Many of the effects of glial Hnmt deletion on motility were sex-specific with a greater impact in males. Ca2+ imaging experiments in the colon myenteric plexus showed that deleting glial Hnmt decreased neuron responses in orally and anally oriented synaptic motor pathways. The differences observed in colon contractility and neuron responses to synaptic pathway stimulation were lost when samples from glial Hnmt knockout mice were incubated with the H3 receptor antagonist clobenpropit. These observations show that histamine clearance by enteric glial Hnmt is important to maintain normal motility by buffering the effects of histamine on enteric neurons. These results suggest that changes to glial histamine clearance may contribute to gut dysfunction in common disorders of gut-brain interaction that involve elevated histamine.

title: Perioperative Nerve Blockade for Acute Postoperative Pain Management After Major Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.
abstract: The efficacy of nerve blockade for perioperative pain management in oral and maxillofacial surgery remains inadequately explored. This study investigated whether perioperative nerve blockade reduces acute postoperative pain (POP) following oral and maxillofacial surgery. Medical records of patients who underwent oral and maxillofacial surgery were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were classified into the "block group" (nerve blockade for major surgery: surgical field diameter ≥ 3 cm, procedure time ≥ 30 min, or surgical field ≤ 5 mm from the inferior alveolar canal) and the "no-block group" (no nerve blockade for minor surgery: surgical field diameter 5 mm from the canal). Visual analog scale (VAS; 0-100 mm) pain intensity; VAS areas under the curves (VASAUCs; mm × day); VASAUCs at postoperative hours 6 (VASAUC_6), 12 (VASAUC_12), 18 (VASAUC_18), and 24 (VASAUC_24); analgesic requirement period (days); and number of days with pain (days) were analyzed. A total of 183 patients were included, including 55 in the block group (114 men and 69 women; median age, 45.0 [29.0-60.5] years). Surgical duration and blood loss were significantly greater in the block group. Although VASAUC_24, overall VASAUC, analgesic requirement period, and number of days with pain were significantly higher in the block group than in the no-block group, no significant between-group differences were observed in VASAUC_6, VASAUC_12, or VASAUC_18. Acute POP outcomes following major surgery with nerve blockade were comparable to those following minor surgery without nerve blockade. These findings suggest that perioperative nerve blockade is potentially effective for managing acute POP after major oral and maxillofacial surgery.

title: Subcortical zone: A transient structure with lasting impact on evolution, circuit assembly and cognitive functions.
abstract: The cortical subplate (SP) is one of the first structures formed during mammalian cerebral cortical development. Our conceptualization of the SP has evolved from a transient developmental region to a multifunctional hub in which the remaining cells perform active functions related to arousal, attention, and brain-state regulation. During development, the SP provides a scaffold enabling thalamic projections to cross the pallial subpallial boundary, accumulate, indirectly and directly interact with intrinsic synaptic networks, and finally enter the cortical plate. Its rich extracellular matrix and dynamic circuitry facilitate rapid plasticity during critical developmental windows, providing a transient synaptic relay for thalamocortical and corticocortical axons while simultaneously supporting radial and tangential neuronal migration, lamination, and cortical arealization. Developmental molecular gradients within the SP align with prospective cortical territories, providing transient circuits that match spontaneous and sensory-driven activity during development, where intrinsic patterning is refined by thalamic input. While all mammals have SP-analogous cell populations, comparative neuroanatomy and cross-species volume, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have revealed laminar and regional differences within the SP. In marsupials, while the SP is more continuous with the cortical plate, SP-analogous neurons are nevertheless present. In carnivores and in pigs, the SP is proportionally larger. In rodents, a subset of SP neurons persists into adulthood as a compact layer 6b at the base of the mature cortex; this layer is characterized by elaborate cortical and extracortical connectivity while exhibiting sensitivity to neuromodulators including orexin, dopamine, serotonin, and neurotensin. These properties similarly emerge in analogous white matter interstitial neurons in primates, thus implicating SP-derived neurons in the regulation of critical brain states such as attention, arousal, sleep-wake cycles, anxiety, and psychedelic-induced experiences. Furthermore, elaborated SP expansion in humans may lend itself to more protracted cortical development and support species-specific changes leading to higher cognitive capacities. The dual role of the SP as an early-maturing developmental scaffold and as an extensive neuromodulatory hub through adulthood confers a potential central role for remnant populations in the etiology of neuropsychiatric diseases, with conceivable origins including but not being limited to heightened vulnerability to hypoxia-ischemia and prematurity. Together, insights to date and ongoing research efforts implicate the SP as a crucial node in human brain development, evolution, and disease.

title: EIF2AK2-Related Disorder Presenting as Progressive Childhood-Onset Generalized Dystonia.
MACSima imaging cyclic staining technology for stem cell-derived graft composition analysis in a model of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-based therapies are promising treatments for Parkinson's disease (PD), with ongoing clinical trials demonstrating the feasibility of transplanting dopaminergic (DA) progenitor cells. Mature grafts are typically assessed using histology- or transcriptomics-based approaches; however, traditional histology-based imaging is limited by the number of markers that can be analyzed simultaneously, while transcriptomic approaches lack spatial resolution or fail to capture protein expression and cell morphology. Here, we characterized hPSC-derived intracerebral DA grafts in a preclinical rat PD model using the MACSima® platform. Cyclic staining combined with marker erasure enabled identification and quantification of the graft components: DA neurons, astrocytes, and vascular leptomeningeal cells (VLMCs). Multi-marker analysis revealed a clear spatial segregation of DA neurons and VLMCs within the graft.

title: Intraindividual Fluctuations of Neurofilament Light Chain in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Implications for Repeated Measurements.
abstract: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is increasingly used for prognostication, trial stratification, and pharmacodynamic monitoring in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). We sought to quantify intraindividual serum NfL fluctuation, estimate individual base NfL levels, and evaluate prediction intervals for distinguishing natural fluctuation from treatment-related change. Three complementary cohorts were analyzed: a multicenter longitudinal cohort from 18 centers (cohort A, 2,548 patients with 9,274 NfL measurements), a prospective high-frequency sampling cohort (cohort B, 18 patients with 77 measurements), and a validation cohort of patients with superoxide dismutase 1-associated ALS receiving tofersen (cohort C, 19 patients with 581 measurements). In cohort A (n = 2,548), intraindividual NfL fluctuations of >30%, >50%, and >100% occurred in 40.2%, 17.1%, and 3.2% of consecutive repeat measurements, respectively. Increasing the number of measurements from 2 to 4 reduced the model-based standard error from 14.6 pg/ml (95% credible interval 13.4-15.9) with 2 measurements to 9.7 pg/ml (95% credible interval 8.8-10.6) with 3 measurements, and 6.6 pg/ml (95% credible interval 5.9-7.4) with 4 measurements. Faster ALS progression was associated with greater NfL fluctuation. In cohort B, 26.8% of weekly paired measurements differed by >30%. In cohort C, standard error-based prediction intervals distinguished intraindividual fluctuation from tofersen-related NfL reductions. Intraindividual NfL fluctuation is common in ALS and may confound interpretation of single NfL measurements. Repeated NfL measurements improve estimation of the individual base NfL level, whereas patient-specific prediction intervals provide a practical framework for interpreting NfL measurements in both clinical practice and ALS trials. ANN NEUROL 2026 ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Once-Daily Modified-Release Pregabalin in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain: A Relevant Addition to Future Consensus Updates.
abstract: Once-daily modified-release pregabalin formulations are clinically relevant therapeutic options that deserve consideration in future updates of the recently published consensus on the use of pregabalin in peripheral neuropathic pain. This letter discusses the clinical evidence supporting these formulations, highlighting their potential role in treatment simplification while acknowledging differences between products and limitations in the available evidence. A prolonged-release formulation has demonstrated non-inferiority to immediate-release pregabalin in painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy, whereas a distinct controlled-release formulation has demonstrated efficacy in postherpetic neuralgia. Incorporating a formulation-specific discussion into future consensus updates could provide a more comprehensive overview of therapeutic options and support individualized management of peripheral neuropathic pain.

title: A Neurobiological Model of Endometriosis-Associated Pain: Stress, Neuroimmune Dysfunction, and Endocannabinoid Signaling.
abstract: Endometriosis-associated chronic pelvic pain is a multidimensional pain condition involving persistent peripheral nociceptive input, peripheral and central sensitization, and substantial psychological distress. However, the neurobiological mechanisms linking chronic pain, stress, and affective disturbances remain incompletely understood. This narrative review synthesizes human and preclinical evidence on the interactions among nociceptive processing, neuroimmune signaling, and stress-response systems in endometriosis-associated pain. Particular attention is given to the autonomic nervous system, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and endocannabinoid system as interconnected regulators of stress adaptation, inflammation, and endogenous pain modulation. Available evidence suggests that lesion-derived inflammatory and nociceptive signaling may initiate peripheral and central sensitization, while persistent pain and chronic stress may alter autonomic, neuroendocrine, and endocannabinoid function. These changes may impair endogenous pain regulation, sustain neuroimmune activation, and influence neural pathways involved in affective processing, potentially reinforcing pain and psychological distress. We propose an integrated neuroimmune-endocrine model in which reciprocal interactions between peripheral nociception and dysregulated central stress- and pain-regulatory systems may contribute to pain persistence beyond peripheral disease activity. Although the proposed relationships remain largely associative and require longitudinal and mechanistic validation, this framework identifies shared neural and neuroimmune pathways that may inform future investigations of pain chronification and the development of mechanism-directed interventions.

title: The foreign language effect on moral judgements of blameworthy and praiseworthy behaviours across moral foundations.
journal: The British journal of social psychology
abstract: The moral foreign language effect (MFLE)-the tendency for moral judgements to differ between native and foreign language contexts-is well documented for blameworthy behaviours, but less is known about whether it extends to praiseworthy behaviours, different moral foundations, or its mechanisms. Across two pre-registered studies with Chinese-English bilinguals (Study 1: N = 100; Study 2: N = 96), we used concise phrases to systematically examine the MFLE in judgements of blameworthy and praiseworthy behaviours, its cross-foundation variability, and potential mediators. Replicating prior work, foreign language attenuated moral judgements of blameworthy behaviours in both studies. Crucially, Study 2 revealed that foreign language use also attenuated moral judgements of praiseworthy behaviours, with effects varying across moral foundations. Mediation analyses suggested that emotional valence was an important but not exclusive mediator of the MFLE, whereas emotional arousal, vividness, and confidence showed more condition-specific patterns; group identity did not mediate. Additionally, representational similarity analysis indicated that the overall relational pattern of moral judgements was broadly shared across native and foreign language conditions. Machine-learning classification showed that dominant emotion types remained largely consistent across languages. These findings broaden the scope of the MFLE and suggest that it may be supported by multiple, partly context-dependent mechanisms.

title: Combination Antiretroviral Therapy in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Targeting HML-2: Non-randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: A subset of individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) have activation of an endogenous retrovirus, HML-2, which has been implicated in the pathogenesis of the disease. Antiretroviral therapies (ART) developed against human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) have some efficacy against HML-2 in vitro. We used combination ART (tenofovir alafenamide, darunavir, ritonavir, and dolutegravir) to determine their safety in ALS and impact on HML-2. Effects on several pathogenic markers and clinical outcome measures were explored. A total of 122 individuals with ALS were screened, 34 were enrolled, 30 were treated and 20 completed 24 weeks of treatment. HML-2 levels and markers of neurodegeneration and immune dysfunction were measured in serum and/or neuron-derived extracellular vesicles (NDEs) isolated from serum. Clinical assessments were performed using the ALS Functional Rating Scale, Revised (ALSFRS-R). Individuals with ≥20% decrease in HML-2 levels were considered a virological responder. There were no serious adverse events. Transient gastrointestinal upset was common. HML-2 levels decreased at 12 and 24 weeks (30.7% ± 28.7%; p = 0.0001) but rebounded 4 weeks after stopping therapy. NDEs showed a decrease of HML-2 RNA (p = 0.02) and TDP-43 levels (p = 0.03) at 24 weeks. There was no significant change in levels of neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein, cytokines, or rate of change of ALSFRS-R scores. Proteomics analysis at baseline identified 5 proteins from which a composite score was developed that predicted individuals who showed a virological treatment response. This should be considered hypothesis generating. The study identifies challenges in conducting clinical trials with ART in ALS. We have developed several bioassays for monitoring effects of treatment and identifying individuals likely to show a virological response to ART. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Itchy Skin-Spinal Sensitization for C-Fibre Input in Healthy Subjects.
abstract: Although spinal itch sensitization is well established for mechanically evoked alloknesis and hyperknesis mediated by Aβ- and Aδ-fibres, the contribution of C-fibre input remains unclear. We investigated whether selective C-fibre activation can evoke itch during pruritogen-induced sensitization and whether this depends on ongoing pruriceptive input. In four cohorts (N = 22, 10, 15, and 15), itch was induced by histamine (CMi-fibres) or cowhage (CM-fibres). Sinusoidal and half-sine-wave stimulation was applied to sensitized and control skin, and itch and pain responses were assessed. Preferential C-fibre activation was validated using selective A-fibre block. Pruritogen pretreatment markedly increased the likelihood of classifying C-fibre stimulation as itchy at sensitized sites compared with native skin (GLMM, Sidak-corrected; all p < 0.0001), whereas itch was rarely evoked contralaterally. Electrically evoked itch did not scale with stimulus intensity, while pain ratings showed robust intensity dependence. Electrical mapping revealed a secondary zone of 'itchy skin' comparable in size to mechanically evoked alloknesis and hyperknesis and exceeding primary afferent receptive fields. Local cooling significantly reduced histamine-induced itch (paired t-test, p = 0.031) and decreased the likelihood of perceiving C-fibre stimulation as itchy (binomial GLMM, odds ratio = 3.99, p = 0.026). C-hyperknesis was more prevalent in participants with persisting spontaneous itch than in those in whom itch had resolved (61.9% vs. 29.2%; p = 0.03). Together, these findings demonstrate that spinal itch sensitization extends to C-fibre input and is dynamically maintained by ongoing pruriceptive activity. This study provides the first evidence that spinal sensitization in humans extends to C-fibre-mediated itch. Selective activation of C-fibre classes induced secondary 'C-hyperknesis,' dependent on ongoing pruriceptive input and rapidly reversible once this input ceased. These findings reveal a dynamic spinal gating mechanism linking pain and itch sensitization. Clinically, they suggest that sustained C-fibre activity may contribute to central sensitization and spreading of itch in chronic pruritus.

title: Manual and Automatic Quantification of Lateral Ventricular CSF Volume in CT Scans, Before and After Shunt Surgery in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus Patients.
journal: Journal of neuroimaging : official journal of the American Society of Neuroimaging
abstract: Increased lateral ventricular volume is a hallmark of idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH). While most research focuses on MRI, CT is widely used in clinical practice. This study compared manual and automated segmentations of lateral ventricular CSF volume on CT and evaluated postoperative volume changes and associations with clinical response. Forty-nine patients with iNPH and paired pre- and postoperative CT examinations were included from Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden. CT images acquired before and after shunt insertion were analyzed using manual segmentations and ScanDx, an AI-driven brain CT segmentation pipeline. Clinical assessment was performed before and 3 months after surgery using the Swedish iNPH scale by Hellström, with cognitive evaluation replaced by the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Forty patients with complete follow-up were classified as responders (n = 30) or nonresponders (n = 10). Manual and automated lateral ventricular volumetry were strongly correlated, with Spearman correlation coefficients of r = 0.93 preoperatively and r = 0.86 postoperatively. Automated segmentations showed systematic bias, with overestimation in specific anatomical regions, including periventricular areas with white matter changes. Median lateral ventricular volume reduction at 6 weeks after shunt surgery was 13.5 mL (12.18%) in manual and 21.5 mL (12.23%) in automated measurements. Clinical response was observed in 75% of patients. Automated CT-based lateral ventricular volume segmentation showed Strong correlation with manual segmentation. However, quality control and cautious interpretation are warranted due to systematic overestimation. Clinical response was observed in 75% of patients; however, magnitude of ventricular volume reduction did not correlate with clinical improvement.

title: The GP behind the screen: from occupational stress to staying ahead - motivation for a virtual primary care career, a qualitative interview study.
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: This study explores the motivations behind physicians' career choices to work in virtual primary care. General practitioners and residents were purposively selected for individual interviews. Data were collected in 2018 and 2019. Transcripts were analysed using Systematic Text Condensation. Setting A public virtual care clinic within primary health care in the Västra Götaland Region, Sweden. Subjects A purposive sample of ten specialists and residents in general practice. Occupational stress in primary care appears to motivate seeking assignments in virtual-only clinics, with prospects of improved work-life balance. Openness to experience and an evolving context create opportunities for development, which in turn motivate engagement in virtual care. The career choice is driven by a desire to stay involved, stay ahead, or not be left out. Individuals' patient-oriented thinking, reflected in a shift from associating virtual care with commercial enterprises to viewing it as a field for improvement, also motivates them. Personal and collective accountability for medically safe and viable virtual care within publicly run primary care fosters a sense of purposeful and responsible career choice, even when the field is otherwise perceived as controversial. GPs' decisions to work in virtual primary care are shaped by multiple, interacting factors and are not necessarily driven by an inherent preference for the virtual format. Virtual care may offer opportunities for professional development, flexibility and a more sustainable working situation. The choice should be understood not only as an attraction to a new mode of care delivery, but also in relation to GPs' broader professional experiences, needs and working conditions.

title: Co-design in childhood-onset disability and disorders: A practical orientation for clinicians and researchers.
abstract: Co-design engages stakeholders as equal partners in the design process and has grown considerably in paediatric health care, education, and technology development. Yet methodological development remains uneven: rich guidance exists for autism and learning disability contexts, while cerebral palsy and other childhood-onset conditions involving complex motor, cognitive, and communication needs have received less systematic attention. This article aims to orient researchers and clinicians in childhood-onset disabilities and disorders to co-design by distinguishing design process models, participatory methods, and techniques, and by examining how co-design has been applied across domains of functioning, that is, motor, cognition, communication, and participation. Drawing on participatory design research and emerging applications in childhood-onset disabilities and disorders, we offer practical guidance that addresses recurring challenges: managing authority dynamics between clinicians and families, avoiding tokenistic participation, adapting session methods for complex needs, and structuring proxy involvement when children and adolescents cannot participate directly.

title: Tele-Yoga and Psychosocial Education for Stress and Work-Life Balance in Remote IT Professionals During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress
abstract: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of an integrated tele-yoga and psychosocial education intervention (Y-PSE) compared with psychosocial education alone (PSE) in reducing perceived stress and improving occupational mental health among 150 IT professionals working remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants were randomized equally to Y-PSE (n = 75) and PSE (n = 75) and assessed over 12 weeks. The primary outcome was perceived stress (PSS-4); secondary outcomes included work engagement, work-life balance, well-being (WHO-5), coping, and sleep quality (PSQI). Analyses included intention-to-treat population, a per-protocol sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with ≥ 75% attendance and completed follow-up assessments, and mediation analyses examining work engagement and work interference with personal life (WIPL) as potential mediators. Y-PSE reduced perceived stress versus PSE (AMD -0.73; 95% CI -1.37 to -0.09; p = 0.026), increased work engagement (AMD 0.55; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.87; p = 0.001), and reduced work interference with personal life (WIPL; AMD -0.42; 95% CI -0.65 to -0.20; p < 0.001). Well-being and coping improved significantly, whereas sleep quality did not differ (p = 0.28). Per-protocol sensitivity analysis yielded directionally consistent findings with larger effect estimates. Work engagement and WIPL were potential mediators, together accounting for most of the reduction in perceived stress. The intervention showed high compliance, feasibility, and potential to address occupational stress through a digital, scalable delivery model. These findings highlight the benefits of combining Yoga with Psychosocial education, underscoring the role of tele-Yoga in mitigating pandemic-related work stress and promoting mental health among remote workers.

title: Impulsivity and Alcohol Use in Young Adults: An EMA Study on Momentary Antecedents.
abstract: Impulsivity is a frequently discussed risk factor for alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the within-person dynamics of momentary impulsivity and alcohol consumption (AC) remain poorly understood, particularly in clinical populations. This study examined whether within-person increases in momentary impulsivity predicted AC probability and quantity and whether situational social context moderated this association. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study with five prompts every other day between 5 pm and 10 pm over 6 weeks. Sixty-one young adults (mean age = 26.5, SD = 4.23; 47.5% women) meeting at least two Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5) criteria for AUD, recruited across Germany. AC (binary: drinking vs. not drinking and quantity in grams), momentary impulsivity and situational social context were assessed at each prompt. Impulsivity was assessed using six items adapted from the Urgency, Premeditation, Perseverance, Sensation Seeking, and Positive Urgency Impulsive Behavior Scale (UPPS-P). Data were analyzed using three-level Bayesian random effect models in Mplus. Contrary to hypothesis, higher momentary impulsivity was associated with a lower probability of AC (b = -0.025, [-0.030, -0.019]) and lower drinking quantity. Prior AC predicted reductions in subsequent impulsivity. Being in the presence of others strongly increased drinking probability, especially when others were drinking. The negative impulsivity-alcohol association was stronger in social contexts. Exploratory subscale analyses indicated that nonplanning and sensation seeking, but not negative urgency, were elevated before drinking onset relative to afterward. Momentary within-person impulsivity predicted reductions in concurrent AC in a clinical AUD sample, challenging dominant theoretical frameworks. Findings highlight the importance of temporal dynamics, social context, and self-medication processes in understanding impulsivity-alcohol associations in everyday life.
